who is the coptic pope now

title: St. Mark the Apostle, founder of our church
text: St. Mark the Apostle brought the Gospel to Egypt and founded the Church of Alexandria, which is why we are called the Church of St. Mark. He wrote the Gospel of Mark, and our Church counts him among the seventy apostles. He also helped other apostles like St. Peter, St. Paul and St. Barnabas. In Alexandria he preached about Jesus, and many people believed and were baptized. He became the first Pope of Alexandria, and he is remembered as a martyr who gave his life for Jesus there. His martyrdom is remembered in the Church on 30 Baramoudah. We thank God for St. Mark and ask for his prayers.

title: The Agpeya and the seven prayers
text: The Agpeya is the Coptic book of the hours. It is our prayer book for seven times in the day, plus a Midnight prayer: Prime in the morning, Terce at the third hour, Sext at the sixth hour, None at the ninth hour, Vespers in the evening, and Compline before bed. Each hour remembers a moment in the life and suffering of Jesus, for example Prime remembers the Resurrection. Every hour has Psalms, a reading from the Gospel and short prayers. The idea of praying seven times a day comes from the Psalm that says, Seven times a day do I praise thee. A good start for a child is to pray Prime in the morning and Compline before bed. You do not have to pray all of them at once. Start small and grow slowly.

verse.text: Seven times a day do I praise thee

title: How do we pray?
text: Praying is simply talking and listening to God, like talking to a loving father. You can pray anywhere and at any time. Start by making the sign of the cross, thank God for good things, say sorry for anything you did wrong, and ask Him for help for yourself and others. Then say Amen. You can pray with your own words, with the Lord's Prayer, or with the prayers in the Agpeya. It is good to have a set time each day, like morning, before meals and before bed. You can stand, sit or kneel. God hears every prayer, even a very short one, and He loves to hear from you.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

verse.text: Pray without ceasing.

title: What is fasting and why do we fast?
text: Fasting means going without some food, or not eating for a period of time, to grow closer to God. It is not a punishment and it is not a diet. In the Coptic Church fasting means giving up meat and other animal products like eggs, milk and cheese. We fast to strengthen our spiritual life and to give our minds and hearts more room for God. Fasting always goes together with prayer and repentance, and we offer it to God alone. Jesus fasted for forty days in the wilderness, and the apostles and the early Church also fasted. The rules for fasting are different for each person based on age and health, so kids should ask Abouna and their parents what is right for them.

title: Fasting on Wednesday and Friday
text: In the Coptic Church we fast on Wednesdays and Fridays during the year. This is a very old practice, and the early Church already kept these two days as fast days. We do not keep the Wednesday and Friday fast during the fifty days after the Resurrection, because that is a time of joy. On a fasting day we give up animal products, like meat, eggs, milk and cheese, and we pray more. The exact rules differ by age and health, and a priest can give an exception when someone needs it. Children should ask Abouna and their parents how much to fast.

title: The Great Lent
text: The Great Lent is the long fast before Easter, when we prepare to remember the death and Resurrection of Jesus. It lasts fifty-five days, and it is the longest fast of the year. It includes the forty days that follow the example of Jesus, who fasted forty days, and it ends with Holy Week. It is a time for more prayer, more kindness, more Bible reading and more giving. During Lent we give up meat and animal products and eat simple foods. A short three day fast, called the Fast of Nineveh, comes a couple of weeks before Lent. The Great Lent is not meant to be sad. It is a hopeful time as we walk with Jesus toward Pascha. Children should ask Abouna and parents what they can fast, since it depends on age and health.

title: The Coptic calendar and Nayrouz
text: The Coptic calendar is the calendar of the Coptic Church, and it comes from the ancient Egyptian calendar. It has thirteen months: twelve months of thirty days, and a little month at the end of five days, or six days in a leap year. The new year begins on the first day of the month of Tout, usually on 11 September. The feast of that day is called Nayrouz, a word that means the beginning of the year. Nayrouz is a day of joy, but the Church also remembers the martyrs, because the Coptic years are counted from the time of the martyrs. Many of our feasts and saint days are counted by the Coptic calendar. Ask Abouna to show you today's date in Coptic.

title: The Holy Family in Egypt
text: When Jesus was a little child, King Herod wanted to harm Him. An angel told Joseph in a dream to take Mary and Jesus and go to Egypt. So the Holy Family traveled to Egypt and stayed there until it was safe to go home. Because Jesus walked on the land of Egypt, the Coptic Church believes Egypt was blessed. The prophet Isaiah also said that the Lord would come to Egypt, and that there would be an altar to the Lord in the land of Egypt. We remember this journey every year, and we thank God for keeping Jesus safe. Many Egyptians love to visit the places where tradition says the Holy Family stayed.

title: Where did the Holy Family stay in Egypt?
text: Church tradition tells us that the Holy Family traveled through many places in Egypt, from the north of the country to the south, and that they were in Egypt for a number of years. Tradition remembers places such as Al-Mataria, Old Cairo, Wadi El Natrun and Al-Muharraq Monastery in Upper Egypt, where tradition says they stayed for a longer time. Many churches in these places honor the visit. Some details come from the tradition of the Church and not from the Bible, so the exact places and the length of time are told in different ways. The Coptic Church celebrates the entrance of the Holy Family into Egypt each year, and we remember it with thanks and joy.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: Who are the martyrs?
text: A martyr is a person who loved Jesus so much that they never stopped believing in Him, even when other people were unkind or made things very hard for them. The word martyr means a witness. The first martyr was St. Stephen the deacon. Many Christians in Egypt were martyrs in the early years of the Church, and they stayed faithful to Jesus. We call them heroes of faith, and we believe they are alive with Christ and happy in heaven. We remember them in church and tell their stories, and we ask for their prayers. We can be brave and faithful like them, by being honest and standing up for what is right.
kw: what happened to the coptic christians
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: Why does the Coptic calendar start from the Era of the Martyrs?
text: The Coptic calendar counts its years from the Era of the Martyrs, which is also called Anno Martyrum. It starts in the year 284 A.D., when the Roman emperor Diocletian came to the throne. During his rule many Christians in Egypt were put to death because they would not give up their faith. The Church chose to start counting from then to honor the martyrs and never forget how faithful they were. So the Coptic year number is lower than the regular year number by about 284 years. Counting this way is a way to say thank you to all those who held on to Christ through hard times.

title: What does Coptic mean?
text: The word Coptic comes from the Greek word for Egypt, and it came to mean the people and the church of Egypt. So the Coptic Church is the church of Egypt, and Copts are the Christians of Egypt. The Coptic language is the last stage of the ancient Egyptian language. It is written with the Greek alphabet plus some extra letters taken from the old Egyptian writing for sounds that Greek does not have. Arabic became the everyday language in Egypt many centuries ago, but Coptic is still the language of the Church, and it is used in the prayers and hymns. Some Copts today learn it again so they can pray in it.

title: Being ready for Holy Communion
text: Holy Communion is the Body and Blood of Jesus, so we get ready for it with care. We try to confess our sins to our priest and be truly sorry for what we did wrong. We make peace with anyone we have upset, because Jesus taught us to be reconciled with our brother before we come to the altar. In the Coptic Church we also fast before Communion, which means we do not eat or drink for a number of hours before we receive, and the length depends on age and health, so ask Abouna. We wash and come to church clean, listen to the Liturgy and pray with respect. If you are not sure whether you are ready, ask Abouna, and he will help you.

title: Saying sorry and being forgiven
text: Everyone makes mistakes, even grown ups. When we do something wrong, that is called sin. God does not want us to hide or feel afraid. He wants us to tell Him we are sorry and try again. This is called repentance. God is full of love, and He forgives us every time we ask from our heart. In confession, we tell our sins to God with Abouna listening, and Abouna prays that God forgives us. Then we feel light and clean. We should also forgive other people, the way God forgives us. Saying sorry is brave, and it makes us stronger and kinder.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

verse.text: If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.

title: How should we behave in church?
text: The church is the house of God, so we come with joy and respect. We arrive on time, dress neatly, and turn off our phones. We make the sign of the cross when we enter and greet people kindly. During the service we listen, sing and pray, and we do not run, shout or play. We do not talk while the Gospel is read or during the prayers. If we need to leave, we do it quietly. When the Haykal curtain opens, we stay still and look at the altar. After the service we can greet Abouna and our friends. Kind and quiet behavior shows that we love Jesus and care for others.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: What is the Bible?
text: The Bible is God's Word, the holy book that tells us about God, His love and His plan to save us. It was written by many people over a long time, but they were inspired by the Holy Spirit. It has two big parts: the Old Testament and the New Testament. The Bible has stories, songs, laws, wise sayings and letters. We read it at home, in Sunday School and in the Liturgy, and the priest explains it. Reading a little each day helps us know God better. The Bible says that God's word is a lamp for our feet and a light for our path.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

verse.text: Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path.

title: The Old and New Testaments
text: The Bible has two parts. The Old Testament tells about the time before Jesus came. It has the stories of creation, Adam and Eve, Noah, Abraham, Moses, David and the prophets, and it has the Psalms and the books of wisdom. It points to Jesus who would come. The New Testament tells about the life of Jesus, the four Gospels of Matthew, Mark, Luke and John, the Acts of the Apostles, the letters of the apostles and the Book of Revelation. The Old and New Testament belong together. The Coptic Church uses the full Old Testament, including the books that some churches leave out, and we read both in church.

title: Who are the angels?
text: Angels are spiritual beings that God created. They are not people who died, and we do not become angels. Angels worship God, bring His messages and take care of us. In the Bible the angel Gabriel told Mary she would have Jesus, and angels guarded people like Daniel. We know the names of the archangels Michael, Gabriel and Raphael, and we ask them to pray for us. Each person has a guardian angel, according to our Church tradition. We do not worship angels, we only worship God. When you feel scared, you can say a short prayer and remember that angels are near.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

verse.text: The angel of the LORD encampeth round about them that fear him, and delivereth them.

title: Who are the saints and why do we ask for their prayers?
text: Saints are people who loved God very much and lived holy lives. Now they are alive with Christ in heaven. The Church believes that they still care for us and pray for us. Just like we ask our parents or friends to pray for us, we ask the saints for their prayers. We do not pray to them as gods. We worship only God, and the saints help us by praying with us to Him. The saints include the apostles, the martyrs, the monks and many men and women of faith. We celebrate their feast days, read about their lives, and try to follow their good examples of love, courage and kindness.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: The Cross and Good Friday
text: Good Friday is the day Jesus died on the cross. He did this because He loves us, and He took our sins on Himself so that we could be forgiven and have life with God. It sounds sad, but it is also a day of great love. Jesus did not stay dead. He did this for us all. In the Coptic Church we call the week before Easter Holy Week, and on Good Friday we pray, read the Bible, sing sad hymns, and fast. We make the sign of the cross because the cross shows how much Jesus loves us. The cross is the sign of victory for Christians.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: The Resurrection
text: On the third day after Jesus died, He rose from the dead. This is the Resurrection, the greatest event in our faith. Early on Sunday morning, the women came to the tomb and found it empty, and an angel told them Jesus had risen. Then Jesus appeared to His disciples and many others, and they were filled with joy. By rising, Jesus defeated death and gave us hope of eternal life. We celebrate this at Easter, which we call the Feast of the Resurrection or Pascha, with a joyful Liturgy at night and a big family meal. We greet each other with Christ is risen, and answer, Truly He is risen.
kw: did jesus rise from the dead

verse.text: He is not here: for he is risen, as he said.

title: How many sacraments are there?
text: The Coptic Orthodox Church has seven sacraments. A sacrament is a holy gift of God, where we receive His grace through the Church. The seven sacraments are Baptism, Chrismation with the Holy Myron, the Eucharist or Holy Communion, Repentance and Confession, the Unction of the Sick, Matrimony, and the Priesthood. Baptism and Chrismation are received one time. We can receive Communion and Confession many times. Each sacrament has its own card in Lumi, so you can ask about any of them.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: What are the seven major feasts of the Lord?
text: Our Church keeps seven great feasts of the Lord, all about Jesus. They are the Annunciation, when the angel told St. Mary the good news. Then the Nativity, when Jesus was born. Then Epiphany, also called Theophany, when Jesus was baptized and the Holy Trinity appeared. Then Palm Sunday, when the people welcomed Jesus into Jerusalem. Then Easter, the Resurrection, when Jesus rose from the dead. Then the Ascension, when Jesus went up to heaven forty days after He rose. And finally Pentecost, fifty days after the Resurrection, when the Holy Spirit came down on the disciples. Each one tells a part of the story of how God saved us. Some of these feasts have the same date every year, and some move, because they depend on the date of Pascha.

title: What are the seven minor feasts of the Lord?
text: Besides the seven major feasts, the Church keeps seven smaller feasts of the Lord. They are the Circumcision of Jesus, the first miracle at the wedding in Cana, the Presentation of Jesus in the Temple (also called Candlemas), Covenant Thursday (Maundy Thursday), St. Thomas Sunday, the entry of the Holy Family into Egypt, and the Transfiguration. We call them minor only because there are fewer special hymns and readings for them, not because they matter less. Each one lets us remember a special moment in the life of Jesus. If you want to learn more about one of them, ask Lumi about it by name, for example the Transfiguration or the wedding at Cana.

title: Why is Christmas on January 7?
text: Many people celebrate Christmas on December 25, but our Church keeps it on 29 Kiahk, which is January 7 on the calendar most people use today. It is not a different Christmas. Long ago the whole Church kept it on the same day. Later the world changed to a new calendar, but our Church kept the older calendar, called the Julian calendar, which the Coptic calendar is close to. Because the two calendars drifted apart by about thirteen days, our Christmas lands on January 7. Nobody knows the exact day Jesus was born. What matters is that we celebrate that God became a man to save us. So on 29 Kiahk, we sing, pray and rejoice together.

title: What is Paramoun?
text: Paramoun is a word for the eve, the day just before a big feast. Our Church has a Paramoun before Christmas and a Paramoun before Epiphany. On these days we fast, and we pray and read the Bible together, so our hearts are ready for the feast the next day. It is a little like getting your room ready before special guests come. Then when the feast arrives, we celebrate with joy. The Paramoun reminds us that waiting and preparing is part of the celebration. Ask Abouna or your parents what the Paramoun fast looks like for kids, because the rules depend on each person's age and health.

title: What is St. Thomas Sunday?
text: St. Thomas Sunday is the Sunday after Easter. On the evening of the Resurrection, Jesus appeared to the disciples, but Thomas was not there. When they told him, Thomas said he would only believe if he saw Jesus and touched His wounds. A week later, Jesus came again, and Thomas was with them. Jesus showed Thomas His hands and side, and Thomas said, 'My Lord and my God.' Jesus then said that people who believe without seeing are blessed. That includes us! We have not seen Jesus with our eyes, but we believe in Him and we know He is alive. The Church remembers this story on St. Thomas Sunday each year.

verse.text: Jesus saith unto him, Thomas, because thou hast seen me, thou hast believed: blessed are they that have not seen, and yet have believed.

title: What is Covenant Thursday (Maundy Thursday)?
text: Covenant Thursday is the Thursday of Holy Week. On this night Jesus ate the Last Supper with His disciples. He gave them His Body and Blood in bread and wine, the first Eucharist, and promised a new covenant, which is a special promise of love between God and His people. Jesus also washed the feet of His disciples to show that we should serve one another humbly. After supper He went to the garden to pray. In the Coptic Church, on this day the priest washes the feet of some people, as a reminder of Jesus washing His disciples' feet, and we remember the Holy Communion that Jesus gave us.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: What is Holy Saturday?
text: Holy Saturday is the day between Good Friday and Easter. On Friday Jesus died on the cross and His body was placed in a tomb. On Saturday the disciples were sad and waited. But the Church knows what happens next, so this day is quiet but full of hope. The Church reads from the Bible about God's promises and the story of how God saves His people. Then, in the night, the Church celebrates the Resurrection Liturgy and the joy of Easter begins. Some people call this day Bright Saturday, because the light of the Resurrection is just about to shine. It teaches us that after waiting and sadness, God brings great joy.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: Why do we pray so much in Holy Week?
text: Holy Week is the most important week of the church year. We remember the last days of Jesus: His entry into Jerusalem, the Last Supper, His arrest, His death on the cross, and His burial. So many families go to church every day, and the services are long. We hear the Gospel stories read slowly and we pray special prayers, and the hymns sound different and quiet. It is like walking with Jesus step by step. We are not only listening to a story from long ago. We are showing God that we love Him and that we are thankful for all He did for us. And then the week ends with the joy of the Resurrection.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: What are the fifty days after Easter?
text: After the Resurrection comes a happy season of fifty days, from Easter until Pentecost. In these days we celebrate that Jesus is alive! The Church does not keep the Wednesday and Friday fast during this time, and the prayers and hymns are joyful. During these fifty days we remember how Jesus appeared to His disciples, how He went up to heaven on the fortieth day in the Ascension, and how the Holy Spirit came upon the disciples on the fiftieth day at Pentecost. It is like one long Sunday of joy. The fifty days teach us that the Resurrection is not only for one day, it is a joy that goes on and on.

title: Why does Easter move to a different date each year?
text: Christmas is on the same day every year, but Easter, called Pascha in our Church, moves. The Church sets the date of Pascha each year by an ancient method, and the date of Pascha changes the dates of other things too. Great Lent starts fifty-five days before Pascha. Palm Sunday is the Sunday before. The Ascension is forty days after the Resurrection and Pentecost is fifty days after. So we call these 'moveable' feasts. Feasts that always stay on the same date, like the Annunciation and the Nativity, are called fixed feasts. If you want to know when Pascha is this year, look at the Church calendar or ask Abouna.

title: What are the months of the Coptic year?
text: The Coptic year has thirteen months. Twelve months have thirty days each. The thirteenth month is very short, only five days, and six days every fourth year. The months are Tout, Baba, Hatour, Kiahk, Tobah, Amshir, Baramhat, Baramouda, Bashans, Paoni, Epep, Mesra, and the little month Nasie. The new year starts on 1 Tout, the day of Nayrouz. Many feasts are named with a Coptic date, like the Nativity on 29 Kiahk and the Annunciation on 29 Baramhat. Some spellings of the month names change in English, so you may see Babah, Hator or Meshir. They are all the same months.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

verse.text: and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days, and years:

title: Where did the Coptic calendar come from?
text: The Coptic calendar grew out of the very old calendar of the ancient Egyptians. The people of Egypt watched the Nile, the great river, and counted the seasons of the year by the time of the flood, the planting and the harvest. Over many years their way of counting was improved, and later the Christians of Egypt used it for their church year and gave it saints and feasts. That is why it is a special part of our heritage. Our feasts and saints' days are written with the Coptic dates. Today, the Coptic calendar is still used by the Church and by Egyptian farmers. When we use it, we remember the faith of the Copts through many years.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: Why is Sunday special?
text: Sunday is the first day of the week, and it is the day that Jesus rose from the dead. That is why Christians have worshiped on Sunday since the time of the apostles. We call it the Lord's Day. Every Sunday is a little Easter! On Sunday we go to church, pray the Holy Liturgy, and receive the Holy Communion, and we do not fast in the way that we do on Wednesday and Friday. Sunday is also a good day to rest, to be with family, and to thank God for the week. The Bible says that this is the day which the Lord has made, and we should be glad in it.

verse.text: This is the day which the LORD hath made; we will rejoice and be glad in it.

title: What can I eat when we are fasting?
text: When the Church fasts, we give up meat and animal products, which means no eggs, milk, butter, cheese or yogurt. Fish is allowed only in some fasts. So what can we eat? Lots of tasty food! Rice, pasta, beans, lentils, falafel, koshary, vegetables, fruits, bread, nuts, and olive oil are all fine. Some families call this 'vegan food'. Fasting is not about the food being yucky. It is about learning to say no to what we want, so we can say yes to God. Always ask your parents and Abouna what is right for you, because kids, sick people, and others may fast in a lighter way.

title: Do kids have to fast?
text: Fasting is for everyone in the Church, but it is not the same for each person. Little children, people who are sick, and others who need strength may fast in an easier way. A child may give up a favorite treat or a bit of screen time instead of a whole meal. A child's parents and Abouna help decide what is right. The important thing is to start learning to fast with love, and to pray while fasting. It is never meant to hurt us. As we grow, we can fast more, step by step, the same way we learn to ride a bike. Ask your parents and your Abouna to help you choose a good fast.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: Is fasting only about food?
text: No! Fasting is not only about food. Fasting means we are giving up something to grow closer to God. The prophet Isaiah taught that a fast God loves is when we are kind to people who are poor, set people free from being treated badly, and share our bread with the hungry. So while we fast from certain foods, we also try to fast from bad words, from fighting, from being greedy and from being unkind. And we add something good: more prayer, more Bible reading, and more love. A fast with kindness is the best fast. If you only skip food but are mean to your sister, you have missed the point of fasting.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

verse.text: Is not this the fast that I have chosen? to loose the bands of wickedness, to undo the heavy burdens, and to let the oppressed go free, and that ye break every yoke?

title: Why do we not eat before Holy Communion?
text: We receive the Body and Blood of Jesus in Holy Communion, so we get ready with respect. In our Church, people who will take Communion keep a fast beforehand and do not eat or drink after a certain time before the Liturgy. That way Jesus is the very first thing that goes into our body that morning. It is a way to show Him that He is more important than breakfast. We also get ready by confessing, praying, and forgiving others. Little children and people who are sick may have different rules, so ask your parents and Abouna how long to fast before Communion. They will help you.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: Why do we feast after we fast?
text: In our Church, fasting and feasting go together like night and day. We fast to prepare, and then we celebrate with joy. After the Nativity Fast comes Christmas. After Great Lent comes Easter. After a fast we are very thankful for the feast, and the food tastes extra good! The feast is not only about eating though. It is about the greatest gift, that Jesus was born, died and rose for us. We go to church, sing hymns, visit family, share food with others and give gifts to those who need them. Fasting teaches us to wait, and the feast teaches us to be thankful and happy in God.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: What are all the fasts in the Coptic year?
text: The Coptic Church has many fasting times. Great Lent before Pascha lasts fifty-five days. The Nativity Fast before Christmas lasts forty-three days. The Apostles Fast comes after Pentecost. The Fast of Nineveh is three days. The Fast of St. Mary is fifteen days in August. There is also Paramoun, the eve of Christmas and Epiphany. And every Wednesday and Friday we fast, except during the fifty days after Easter. All together, we fast more than two hundred days of the year! That sounds like a lot, but these times of prayer help us grow closer to God, and kids fast in an easy way that their parents and Abouna choose for them.

title: What is the Fraction in the Liturgy?
text: Near the end of the Holy Liturgy, after the priest has prayed over the bread and wine and they have become the Body and Blood of Jesus, the priest breaks the Holy Body into pieces. This is called the Fraction. It is a time when the priest prays a special prayer, and the prayer is different for different feasts and seasons of the year. For example, there are fractions for Christmas, for Easter, for Lent and for the saints. We say 'Kyrie eleison' and listen. It reminds us that Jesus gave Himself for us and that we all share in one Body. After the Fraction, the priest prepares to give Holy Communion to the people.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: Why do we use cymbals and a triangle in church?
text: In many Coptic churches you will hear the cymbals and the triangle. We use them to give praise to God with joy. The Bible says to praise God with cymbals, and it tells us in the Psalms to use many instruments. The cymbals and triangle keep the rhythm for hymns like the Hymn of the Three Saintly Youths and the hymns of Epiphany or Christmas. Deacons and the congregation sing along and clap or keep the beat, and the sound is joyful. Our old Coptic hymns have been passed down from teachers to students for many generations, so when we sing them we join the voices of the Church from long ago.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

verse.text: Praise him upon the loud cymbals: praise him upon the high sounding cymbals.

title: What is Tasbeha, the midnight praise?
text: Tasbeha means 'praise'. It is a service of hymns and prayers to praise God, often held at night or in the early morning, especially before Sunday. We sing the Psalms and the song of Moses, the praise of the Three Young Men, and many hymns to the Lord and to St. Mary and the saints. We do this because the angels praise God all the time, and we want to join them. The Church has prayed through the night for ages, just like the Bible says about the prophets and the apostles who prayed at midnight. Many churches have a Tasbeha service, and kids and youth are welcome to come, to learn the hymns and to praise God.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: What is the Raising of Incense?
text: Before the Holy Liturgy begins, there is a special prayer of incense in the morning, called the Raising of Incense, and a similar one in the evening. The priest holds the censer, where the incense is burning, and walks around the altar, and the people sing hymns and pray. The sweet smoke rising up shows our prayers going up to God, like the Bible says in the Psalms and the book of Revelation. We pray for the whole world, for the Church, for the sick, for travelers, and for peace. Even the morning and evening prayers remind us that we should start and end every day by turning to God.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: Why do we pray in different languages in church?
text: If you go to a Coptic church you might hear Coptic, Arabic, English and sometimes other languages. Coptic is the old language of Egypt, and our oldest hymns and some parts of the Liturgy are still sung in it. We keep it as a treasure from the early Church. Arabic is spoken by many Coptic families in Egypt, and English is spoken by many of us in our country. We use all of them so everyone can understand and join the prayers. It does not matter which language we use, because God understands every language. What matters is that we pray with love, and that we learn what the words mean.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: Why do we stand when the Gospel is read?
text: In the Holy Liturgy, we stand while the Gospel is read. The Gospel is the good news about Jesus, with His words and His works. When the deacon and priest read it, we stand up to listen with respect, as if Jesus Himself is speaking to us. Before the reading, the people say 'Glory be to You, O Lord' and at the end 'Glory be to God forever'. We also light candles and sometimes the priest burns incense and walks around with the Gospel book. This all shows how much we love and honor God's word. It teaches us to listen carefully and to try to do what Jesus says.
kw: glory be to you o lord
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: What is the blessed bread after the Liturgy?
text: At the end of the Holy Liturgy, many churches give out small pieces of blessed bread to everyone. This bread is not the Holy Communion. It is bread that the priest has blessed, and it is a sign of love and fellowship, so that all the people, even those who did not take Communion, share in a loving meal together. In the early Church, Christians shared a meal of love, called the Agape. In some churches this blessed bread is called the Eulogia. It is a nice time to greet your friends, say thank you to Abouna, and share smiles. Always eat it with respect and thankfulness.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: Why do church hymns sound different in different seasons?
text: If you listen closely, you will notice the melodies of our hymns change during the year. In joyful times like Easter and Christmas, the tunes are bright and happy. During Great Lent and especially Holy Week, the tunes are slower and sadder. On Good Friday there are the 'sorrowful' melodies, and then at Easter the joyful ones return. The tunes help us to feel what the Church is remembering. When Jesus suffered we are quiet and solemn. When He rose we sing with joy. The words and the tunes work together to teach us. So when you listen to a hymn, try to hear how it makes you feel, and think about why.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: How does the church year tell the story of Jesus?
text: Our Church year is like a big story that we live every year. It starts with the Coptic New Year at Nayrouz. Then comes the Nativity Fast and Christmas, when Jesus is born. At Epiphany we remember His baptism. Then Great Lent leads to Holy Week, Good Friday and the joy of the Resurrection. After that comes the Ascension, and Pentecost when the Holy Spirit came. Then the Apostles Fast, the summer feasts, and the Fast of St. Mary in August. The year goes round and round, and each time we live the same great story of God's love, hearing it again with new eyes as we grow up. It helps us remember Jesus every day.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: Why do we say Kyrie eleison 41 times?
text: 'Kyrie eleison' means 'Lord, have mercy'. In the Agpeya, at the end of each prayer hour, we say it forty-one times. It is a short prayer that we say slowly and with all our heart. The number is a tradition of the Church. Some say it reminds us of the wounds of Jesus, but the main thing is that when we repeat the prayer, we calm down and ask God for help and forgiveness. You do not need a lot of words to pray. Even kids can say 'Lord, have mercy' when they feel scared, sorry, or worried. God always listens to us and loves us. Try saying it quietly before bed tonight.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: How does each Agpeya hour begin?
text: Each hour of the Agpeya starts in a similar way. We stand, make the sign of the cross, and begin with 'In the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, one God. Amen.' Then we thank God, as the first thing, with the Thanksgiving prayer. After that we pray Psalm 50, which is Psalm 51 in many Bibles, where King David asks God for mercy and forgiveness. Then come the psalms and the Gospel for that hour, and prayers. Each hour ends with 'Lord, have mercy' forty-one times and the Lord's Prayer. When you pray, start with thanks, then say sorry, then ask. This is a good pattern for your own prayers too.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

verse.text: Have mercy upon me, O God, according to thy lovingkindness: according unto the multitude of thy tender mercies blot out my transgressions.

title: What is the Synaxarium?
text: The Synaxarium is a book of the lives of the saints and the feasts of the Church, arranged by day of the Coptic calendar. For each day of each Coptic month, it tells the story of the saints and martyrs we remember that day. In some churches a short reading from it is read at Liturgy, and it is a great way to learn about the heroes of our faith. When a saint's day is written like '11 Tout' or '29 Kiahk', that is the date in the Synaxarium. Kids can read about saints like St. George, St. Mina, and St. Demiana in it. You can ask your servant or Abouna to find your name saint in the Synaxarium.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: What does Abouna mean?
text: Abouna is an Arabic word that means 'our father'. We call our priest Abouna because he is like a spiritual father to us. He prays for us, teaches us, hears our confession, and takes care of our church family, like a father cares for his children. We say Abouna to show love and respect, and we usually add his name, like 'Abouna Mina'. Abouna's wife is called Khouria in Arabic, or Tasoni in Coptic. When you meet Abouna in church, you can greet him and ask for his blessing by crossing your hands. He is happy to help you with questions about God, the Bible and the Church.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: What does Anba mean?
text: Anba is a title in the Coptic Church. It comes from an old word for 'father', and we use it for bishops and also for great monks and saints, like Anba Antonius, Anba Bishoy and Anba Abraam. The Pope has his own title, 'His Holiness', but bishops are usually called Anba and their name. The bishop is a leader in the Church who takes care of many churches in an area, called a diocese, and he ordains priests. So when you hear Anba, think of a spiritual father and a good example of faith who we should respect and learn from.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: What is special about the month of Kiahk?
text: Kiahk is the fourth month of the Coptic year, and it is the month we get ready for Christmas. During Kiahk, many churches hold special evening praises called the Kiahk Tasbeha, where we sing hymns about St. Mary, the Incarnation and the coming of Jesus. The Nativity Fast also runs through Kiahk. Families go to church more often, and children learn the Kiahk hymns. The month ends on the Feast of the Nativity, 29 Kiahk. People sometimes call Kiahk the month of praise, because the Church is filled with songs. It is a lovely season of waiting, and it teaches us to make our hearts a place where Jesus can be born.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: What is Lazarus Saturday?
text: Lazarus Saturday is the day before Palm Sunday. We remember the day Jesus raised His friend Lazarus from the dead. Lazarus had been in the tomb for four days when Jesus came. His sisters, Mary and Martha, were very sad. Jesus wept with them, then called out in a loud voice, Lazarus, come forth, and Lazarus walked out alive. This miracle showed that Jesus is the Lord of life and has power even over death. It also points ahead to His own Resurrection. So just before Holy Week begins, the Church reminds us that Jesus is stronger than death, and that we can trust Him when we are sad or afraid.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: Who is God?
text: God is the One who made everything: the sky, the earth, the animals, and you. God has no beginning and no end, and He is always with us. We cannot see Him, but He sees us and loves us very much. The Bible says, God is love. We believe in one God in three Persons, the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit. We often call the first Person God the Father, because He is the loving Father of all. God is good, strong and kind. He listens when we pray, He takes care of us, and He wants us to be with Him forever. When we feel scared or alone, we can remember that God is near.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

verse.text: God is love.

title: Did God make me? Who made me?
text: Yes! God made you. He made every person with love, and He made you exactly the way He wanted you to be. God knew you before you were born, and He has a special plan for your life. You are not an accident. That is why we say thank you to God for our eyes, our hands, our family and our friends. Your mom and dad helped bring you into the world, and God is the one who gives life to every person. Because God made us, every person is precious to Him, even people who look or sound different from us. We should treat everyone kindly, because God made them too. You are loved.

verse.text: I will praise thee; for I am fearfully and wonderfully made

title: How old is the earth? Did God make the dinosaurs?
text: God made everything. The Bible begins with the words, In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth. Our Church teaches that God is the Creator of the sky, the sea, the land and every living thing. That is the most important thing for us to know and to be thankful for. How and when God made things, and how old the earth is, are questions that scientists study, and they are still learning new things. The Church does not ask children to worry about that. If you love dinosaurs, you can enjoy them and be amazed at how big and wonderful God's creation is. If you have more questions, you can ask Abouna or your teacher. It is good to be curious.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

verse.text: In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.

title: What is the Coptic Orthodox Church?
text: The Coptic Orthodox Church is the Christian church of Egypt. The word Coptic means Egyptian. Our church was founded by St. Mark the Apostle, who brought the good news of Jesus to Alexandria in Egypt, so it is one of the oldest churches in the world. The head of our church is the Pope of Alexandria, who follows St. Mark. We pray the Holy Liturgy, keep the seven sacraments, fast, love the saints and honor St. Mary. Today there are Coptic Orthodox churches in Egypt and all over the world, including right here. Many of our hymns and prayers are very old, and we keep them so that we can pray the way the first Christians did.

title: What does Orthodox mean?
text: Orthodox comes from two old Greek words. One means right or straight, and the other means worship or glory. So Orthodox means right faith and right worship. It means we hold on to the true faith about Jesus that the apostles handed down to the Church, and we worship God the way the Church has worshiped for a very long time. Coptic means Egyptian, as you learned. So Coptic Orthodox means the Orthodox Church of Egypt. Our church keeps the faith that was taught by St. Mark and the great fathers like St. Athanasius and St. Cyril. There are other Orthodox churches around the world too, and we are happy to be part of this family of faith.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: Are there other churches? How are we different?
text: Yes, there are many Christian churches in the world, such as Catholic, Protestant (sometimes called Evangelical) and other Orthodox churches. All Christians love Jesus, believe in Him, and are baptized in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit. We should respect everyone and be kind to all, because Jesus loves them. We are Coptic Orthodox. In our church we keep the traditions we received from the early Church: the seven sacraments, the Holy Liturgy, fasting, praying the Agpeya, using icons, asking the saints to pray for us, and honoring St. Mary the Theotokos. Churches can teach some things differently, and that is a big topic. When you are older, Abouna can explain more, and you can ask him any question you have.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: Who are the twelve apostles?
text: An apostle is someone Jesus sent out to share the good news. Jesus chose twelve men to be close to Him, to learn from Him, and to be sent out to teach the world. They are Peter, Andrew, James the son of Zebedee, John, Philip, Bartholomew, Thomas, Matthew, James the son of Alphaeus, Thaddaeus (also called Jude), Simon the Zealot, and Judas Iscariot. Judas later turned away, and the apostles chose Matthias to take his place. Later Jesus also called St. Paul to be an apostle, and the Church remembers many other apostles too. After the Holy Spirit came at Pentecost, the apostles traveled to many countries and told people about Jesus, and St. Mark brought the message to Egypt.

title: Who was Judas?
text: Judas Iscariot was one of the twelve apostles. He walked with Jesus, heard Him teach, and saw His miracles. But Judas let love of money grow in his heart. He agreed to tell the leaders where to find Jesus, and they paid him thirty pieces of silver. Later he felt very sorry for what he had done. The Bible tells us this sad story so that we can learn from it. We can choose to be loyal to Jesus and to love Him more than anything else. We should never choose money or anything else over Jesus and our friends. If we do make a mistake, we can say sorry to God and ask Him to forgive us. God is always ready to forgive when we come back to Him.

title: Why is Jesus called the Lamb of God?
text: When John the Baptist saw Jesus coming, he said, Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world. A lamb is gentle and quiet, and it is also what the people of the Old Testament offered to God. At the first Passover in Egypt, a lamb was given and the families were kept safe. Jesus is the true Lamb. He gave Himself on the cross out of love, so that our sins could be forgiven and we could live with God. Jesus is also called the Good Shepherd, because He knows His sheep by name and takes care of them. We are His little lambs. That is why Lumi the lamb is a friendly helper in this app: a lamb reminds us of Jesus and of gentleness.

verse.text: Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world.

title: What is a prophet? Who are the prophets?
text: A prophet is a person God chose to speak His word to the people. God gave the prophets messages to tell the people to love Him, to do what is right, and to be ready for the Savior. Some prophets told about Jesus long before He was born. Elijah, Isaiah, Jeremiah, Daniel, Jonah and many others were prophets in the Old Testament. John the Baptist is the last and greatest prophet, because he pointed to Jesus and said, Behold the Lamb of God. Prophets were not always popular, and sometimes they were brave in hard times. We can learn from them to listen to God and to be brave in telling the truth. We read their words in the Bible and in the church readings.

title: What is a miracle?
text: A miracle is something wonderful that only God can do. It goes beyond what people or nature can do on their own. In the Bible, Jesus did many miracles, because He is God and He loves people. He made the blind see, He healed the sick, He calmed the storm, He fed five thousand people with five loaves and two fish, and He raised Lazarus from the dead. These miracles showed His power and His kindness. Many saints also prayed, and God did miracles through them. Miracles still happen today when God answers prayers in ways we do not expect. God is never too small or too far away to help us. We can always pray to Him, and He will answer in the best way.

title: What is a saint? How does someone become a saint?
text: A saint is a holy person who loved God with all their heart and lived close to Him. Saints can be martyrs, monks, teachers, kings, mothers, fathers, or even children. In our church, we remember them and love them, and we ask them to pray for us. The Church does not have one big formal process to make someone a saint. Instead, the Church recognizes saints over time. People see how they lived, how they loved God, and how God worked through them, and the Church honors them. Their stories are read in the Synaxarium on their feast days. You do not need to be famous to be holy. Every one of us is called to become a saint by loving God and others, a little each day.

title: What is faith?
text: Faith means trusting God even when we cannot see Him. We cannot see the wind, but we see the leaves move and we know it is there. In the same way we cannot see God with our eyes, but we know He is with us because of what He has done. After the Resurrection, St. Thomas did not believe until he saw Jesus. Jesus said that those who believe without seeing are blessed. That means us! Faith is not just knowing about God. It is trusting Him when we are afraid, praying to Him, and doing what He asks. Our faith grows when we pray, read the Bible, go to church and take Holy Communion. Even a small faith can grow big.

verse.text: Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen.

title: What is Sunday School?
text: Sunday School is a place in the church where children come together to learn about Jesus, the Bible and our Coptic Orthodox faith. We hear Bible stories, learn about the saints and the feasts, memorize verses, sing hymns, play and make friends. Our teachers are servants. A servant is a person who gives their time to God and to us with love, and they learn together with us. Sunday School helps us to grow in our faith, to know how to pray, and to know the Church better. We also learn how to be kind and honest in our daily lives. Sunday School is a place where everyone is welcome, and where you can ask questions about God and the Church.

title: What are the four Gospels?
text: The word Gospel means good news. The good news is that Jesus came to save us. The four Gospels are the first four books of the New Testament: Matthew, Mark, Luke and John. Each one was written by a person led by the Holy Spirit, and each tells us the story of the life, the teaching, the miracles, the death and the Resurrection of Jesus. Matthew and John were apostles who followed Jesus. Mark and Luke were helpers of the apostles. Each Gospel tells the story in a slightly different way, like four friends describing the same wonderful day. In church, the Gospel is the most honored reading, and we stand while it is read. You can read them yourself in the Bible.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: What is the Temple and the Tabernacle?
text: In the Old Testament, God asked Moses to build a special tent called the Tabernacle, where the people could worship Him. They carried it with them in the desert. Later King Solomon built a beautiful Temple in Jerusalem, and the people came there to pray and bring offerings to God. The Temple was a holy place, because God's presence was with His people there. Our church building is like the Temple and the Tabernacle. It is the house of God, with an altar, incense, a haykal, and holy things. We behave with reverence in church because God is truly with us. Also, we ourselves are the temple of the Holy Spirit when we love God and live in a holy way.

verse.text: And let them make me a sanctuary; that I may dwell among them.

title: Who was King Herod?
text: Herod was a king who ruled Judea when Jesus was born. When the wise men came and asked where the new King of the Jews was, Herod became worried and jealous, because he wanted to stay king. He wanted to harm baby Jesus. But God protected Jesus. An angel told St. Joseph in a dream to take Mary and the child and go to Egypt. So the Holy Family traveled to Egypt, and that is how Egypt was blessed by Jesus' visit. When Herod was gone, the angel told Joseph it was safe, and they went home to Nazareth. This story teaches us that God takes care of us, and that no one can stop His plans. We are thankful that Jesus came to Egypt.

title: Who was Pontius Pilate?
text: Pontius Pilate was the Roman governor of Judea at the time of Jesus. The Jewish leaders brought Jesus to him, and Pilate had to decide what to do. Pilate asked Jesus questions, and he said that he found no fault in Him. But the crowd shouted loudly, and Pilate gave in because he was afraid of the people. He washed his hands in front of the crowd and then allowed Jesus to be crucified. Jesus did this willingly, out of love, to save us. This story teaches us to be brave and to do what is right, even when others around us are doing wrong. Pilate's name is also mentioned in the Creed that we pray in church.

title: What is the fruit of the Spirit?
text: When a tree is healthy, it grows good fruit. When the Holy Spirit lives in us, He makes good things grow in our hearts too. St. Paul wrote about them in his letter to the Galatians. The fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness and self-control. Some of these are easy for us, and some take practice. We cannot grow them by ourselves. The Holy Spirit helps us when we pray, go to church, take Holy Communion and ask Him to help us. You can try one each day. For example, be patient with your brother, be kind to a new friend, or be gentle when you are upset. Over time, your heart will grow lovely fruit.

verse.text: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, meekness, temperance

title: What is the Kingdom of God?
text: The Kingdom of God is where God is King, and where His love and His will are done. Jesus talked about it often. It is not like a kingdom of the world with soldiers and castles. It begins in our hearts when we love God and follow Jesus. It is also the happy life with God in heaven that will last forever. When we pray the Lord's Prayer and say, Thy kingdom come, we are asking that God's love, peace and goodness will grow here on earth too. Jesus said to put God first. We help the Kingdom of God grow when we are kind, tell the truth, forgive, share and pray. Heaven is a part of that Kingdom, where God lives with the angels and saints.

verse.text: But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.

title: What was Jesus like as a boy?
text: The Bible tells us only a little about Jesus as a boy. He grew up in Nazareth with St. Mary and St. Joseph, and He obeyed them. When Jesus was twelve, the family went to Jerusalem for the feast of Passover. On the way home, Mary and Joseph could not find Him. After three days they found Him in the Temple, sitting with the teachers, listening to them and asking questions. Everyone was amazed at how well He understood. Jesus told His mother that He must be in His Father's house. Then He went home with them and obeyed them. The Bible says that Jesus grew in wisdom and in size, and people and God were pleased with Him.

title: Does God love me?
text: Yes! God loves you very much, and He loves you just as you are. The Bible tells us that God is love. He loved us so much that He sent His Son, Jesus, to save us. God loves you when you are happy and when you are sad. He loves you even when you make a mistake, and He is always ready to forgive you when you say sorry. You never have to do anything special to make God love you. His love for you never ends. When we remember how much God loves us, we want to love Him back and to love other people too.

title: What are the Psalms?
text: The Psalms are 150 songs and prayers in the Bible. Many of them were written by King David, who played the harp and sang to God while he took care of his sheep. Some Psalms say thank you to God, some ask for help, and some praise Him with joy. We pray the Psalms in church and in the Agpeya, the book of daily prayers, and we sing them in our hymns. When you are happy, sad or afraid, you can pray a Psalm too. Psalm 23, The Lord is my shepherd, is a favorite of many children.

title: What is the Creed?
text: The Creed is a short prayer that tells what we believe. We say it together in the Holy Liturgy. It starts with the words, We believe in one God, God the Father, the Almighty, Creator of heaven and earth. It tells us that Jesus Christ is the Son of God, that He was born of the Virgin Mary, died on the cross, rose again on the third day and went up to heaven. It speaks about the Holy Spirit, the Giver of life, about one holy Church, about baptism, and about the life of the world to come. The bishops first wrote the Creed at the Council of Nicaea, where St. Athanasius of Alexandria defended the faith that Jesus is truly God.

title: What is the Book of Acts?
text: The Book of Acts tells what happened after Jesus went up to heaven. St. Luke wrote it, the same Luke who wrote the Gospel of Luke. It tells how the Holy Spirit came on the apostles at Pentecost, and how the Church began in Jerusalem and then grew in many countries. You can read about St. Peter, St. Stephen and the journeys of St. Paul, who told people everywhere about Jesus. The book shows us that the Church is a family that prays together, shares and helps each other.

verse.text: But ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses unto me both in Jerusalem, and in all Judaea, and in Samaria, and unto the uttermost part of the earth.

title: What is the Sermon on the Mount?
text: One day Jesus went up on a mountainside, and a big crowd came to listen. He sat down and taught them many things. We call this the Sermon on the Mount. Jesus began with the Beatitudes, which tell who God blesses: people who are gentle, who are sorry for their sins, who are merciful, who have pure hearts and who make peace. He taught us to love our enemies, to pray, to forgive, and to trust God who takes care of the birds and the flowers. He also gave us the golden rule: treat other people the way you want them to treat you. In this teaching Jesus also taught the Lord's Prayer.

verse.text: Therefore all things whatsoever ye would that men should do to you, do ye even so to them

title: Is it okay to feel sad?
text: Yes, it is okay to feel sad sometimes. Everyone feels sad, and even Jesus cried when His friend Lazarus died. God is very close to us when we are sad. You can tell Jesus how you feel in a prayer, using your own words. It also helps to talk to someone you trust, like your mom, dad, servant or Abouna. They love you and want to listen. Feeling sad does not last forever. God gives comfort and joy again, and He is always with you.

title: Isaac and the ram
text: God asked Abraham to show how much he trusted Him. Abraham loved his son Isaac very much, but he trusted God even more. Abraham and Isaac climbed a mountain together carrying wood. Isaac asked where the lamb was, and Abraham answered that God would provide one. Just when Abraham was ready to obey, an angel of the Lord called out and told him to stop. Isaac was safe! Abraham then saw a ram caught in a bush, and God had provided exactly what was needed. The Church also sees this story as a picture of Jesus, God's own Son, who later gave Himself for us. The lesson for us is that God can be trusted, and He always takes care of those who trust Him.

verse.text: My son, God will provide himself a lamb for a burnt offering

title: Jacob's ladder
text: Jacob was traveling alone, far from home, and he was probably feeling worried. When night came he lay down with a stone for a pillow. In a dream he saw a ladder reaching from earth up to heaven, and angels of God going up and down on it. God spoke to Jacob and promised to be with him and keep him wherever he went. When Jacob woke up he said that God was in this place, and he had not known it. He named the place Bethel, which means house of God. We may feel alone sometimes, but God is with us wherever we go, even when we cannot see Him.

verse.text: Behold, I am with thee, and will keep thee in all places whither thou goest

title: Joshua and the walls of Jericho
text: After Moses, God chose Joshua to lead His people into the land He promised them. The city of Jericho had tall, strong walls, and nobody could get in. God gave Joshua a surprising plan. The people did not fight. They walked quietly around the city once a day for six days, with priests carrying the ark and blowing trumpets. On the seventh day they walked around seven times, then the people shouted, and the walls fell down. Joshua obeyed God even when the plan seemed strange. God had told him to be strong and not to be afraid, because He would be with him. When we obey God and trust Him, nothing is too big for Him.

verse.text: Be strong and of a good courage; be not afraid, neither be thou dismayed: for the LORD thy God is with thee whithersoever thou goest.

title: Ruth stays with Naomi
text: Ruth was a young woman whose husband had died. Her mother-in-law Naomi decided to go back to her homeland of Bethlehem, and told Ruth to stay with her own family. But Ruth loved Naomi and said she would go wherever Naomi went, and that Naomi's God would be her God. In Bethlehem, Ruth worked hard gathering leftover grain in the field of a kind man named Boaz. Boaz noticed her goodness and took care of her. Later they married. Ruth became the great-grandmother of King David, and she is named in the family line of Jesus. Her story shows how loyalty, hard work and kindness are rewarded by God.

verse.text: thy people shall be my people, and thy God my God

title: God calls young Samuel
text: Samuel was a boy who helped the old priest Eli in the house of the Lord. One night Samuel heard a voice call his name. He ran to Eli and said, Here I am, but Eli had not called him. This happened three times. Then Eli understood that it was God calling. Eli told Samuel that if he heard the voice again, he should say, Speak, Lord, for your servant is listening. Samuel did, and God spoke to him. Samuel grew up to be a faithful prophet and helped lead God's people. God can speak to children too, and we can listen to Him by praying, reading the Bible and obeying what is good.

verse.text: Speak; for thy servant heareth.

title: Elijah and the ravens
text: Elijah was a prophet who loved God and spoke the truth to a king who did not follow God. There was no rain for a long time, and food became hard to find. God told Elijah to hide by a brook, and God sent ravens to bring him bread and meat each morning and evening. Later God sent him to a poor widow who had only a little flour and oil, and God made her jar and her oil last until the rain came again. God took care of Elijah in surprising ways. Later on Mount Carmel, Elijah prayed and God answered with fire from heaven. The story reminds us that God knows what we need and cares for us.

title: Gideon and the three hundred
text: God's people were being troubled by enemies, and God chose Gideon to help them. Gideon felt small and unsure, but God said He would be with him. Gideon gathered many soldiers, but God said there were too many, so people would think they had won by their own strength. In the end only three hundred men were left. Gideon gave each man a trumpet and a clay jar with a torch hidden inside. At night they blew the trumpets, broke the jars and shouted, and the enemy ran away confused. The victory belonged to God. We do not need to be big or strong, because God can do great things through people who trust Him.

title: Job trusts God
text: Job was a good man who loved God. He had a big family and many animals, and life was happy. Then very hard things happened. He lost his animals, his children and his health. Job was very sad and he did not understand why, and some friends did not comfort him well. But Job never stopped trusting God. He said the name of the Lord should be blessed. In the end God spoke to Job, and God gave him healing and blessed him again with a new family and more than before. Job's story teaches us that when life is sad or confusing, we can still trust that God is near and loves us.

verse.text: the LORD gave, and the LORD hath taken away; blessed be the name of the LORD.

title: Solomon asks for wisdom
text: When Solomon became king after his father David, he was young. One night God said to him in a dream, Ask what I should give you. Solomon could have asked for riches, a long life or power. Instead he asked for an understanding heart so that he could rule God's people well and know right from wrong. God was pleased that he asked for this. God gave him great wisdom, and also gave him the riches and honor he had not asked for. Solomon later built the temple in Jerusalem for God. The story teaches us to ask God first for wisdom and goodness, and to trust Him with the rest.

verse.text: Trust in the LORD with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding.

title: The parable of the sower
text: Jesus told this story to teach how we receive God's word. A farmer went out to scatter seed. Some seed fell on the path, and birds ate it. Some fell on rocky ground with thin soil, and it grew fast but dried up. Some fell among thorns, which choked it. But some fell on good soil and grew into a great harvest. Jesus explained that the seed is God's word. The hearts that are like good soil listen, understand and keep the word, and then they bear fruit by doing good. We can make our hearts good soil by listening in church, reading the Bible, praying and doing what Jesus teaches.

verse.text: Who hath ears to hear, let him hear.

title: The lost coin
text: Jesus told a story about a woman who had ten silver coins and lost one. She did not say it did not matter. She lit a lamp, swept the whole house and searched carefully until she found it. When she found it, she called her friends and neighbors and said to rejoice with her. Jesus said that in the same way there is joy among the angels of God when one person turns back to Him. Every one of us is precious to God, and He does not give up on anyone. If we ever feel lost or have done wrong, God is happy when we come back to Him.

verse.text: Rejoice with me; for I have found the piece which I had lost.

title: Jesus heals blind Bartimaeus
text: Bartimaeus was a blind man who sat by the road near Jericho and asked people for help. When he heard that Jesus was passing by, he called out loudly, Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me! Some people told him to be quiet, but he cried out even more. Jesus stopped and asked for him to be brought. Jesus asked what he wanted, and Bartimaeus said he wanted to see. Jesus told him his faith had made him well, and right away he could see. Then Bartimaeus followed Jesus on the road. His story shows that Jesus hears us when we call, and He cares for everyone, even when others ignore them.

verse.text: Jesus, thou son of David, have mercy on me.

title: Jesus raises Lazarus
text: Lazarus lived in Bethany with his sisters Mary and Martha, and Jesus loved them. When Lazarus became sick and died, his sisters were very sad. By the time Jesus arrived, Lazarus had been in the tomb four days. Jesus saw how sad everyone was, and the Bible says Jesus wept. Jesus told Martha that He is the resurrection and the life. Then He went to the tomb, asked for the stone to be taken away, prayed to the Father, and called with a loud voice, Lazarus, come forth! Lazarus came out alive. This miracle shows that Jesus has power over death and that He cares deeply when we are sad.

verse.text: I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live:

title: Zacchaeus climbs the tree
text: Zacchaeus was a short man who collected taxes in Jericho, and many people did not like him because he had been unfair with money. When he heard Jesus was coming, he wanted to see Him, but the crowd was too tall. So he ran ahead and climbed a sycamore tree. Jesus stopped under the tree, looked up and called him by name. He said He would stay at Zacchaeus's house that day. Zacchaeus was so happy. He promised to give half of what he had to the poor, and to give back four times what he had taken unfairly. Jesus loves us and welcomes us, and when we meet Him our hearts change.

verse.text: For the Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost.

title: Why does the priest wear special clothes?
text: During the Holy Liturgy the priest and the deacons wear special clothes called vestments. They are not for fashion. They are set apart for serving at the altar, just like a special uniform for a special job. The vestments are often white, which is a sign of purity. Our Coptic teaching says the white tunic reminds us of the angels who serve God. The deacon also wears a stole across his shoulder, and it reminds us that a deacon serves like an angel. The colors and crosses on the vestments are beautiful because we are offering our best to God. When we see them, we remember that the Liturgy is heavenly worship and we are joining in with the angels.

title: What is a monastery?
text: A monastery is a place where monks live. Monks are men who give their lives to God, pray many hours a day, work with their hands and live simply, often far from busy cities. Women who do this are called nuns and live in convents. The first monks in the world lived in Egypt, and St. Antony is called the father of monks. Later St. Pachomius started monks living together as a community. Monasteries in Egypt are still alive today, such as in the desert of Wadi El Natrun. Many popes of our church were monks before they became popes. Monks pray for the whole world, and many families visit monasteries to pray and be blessed.

title: Why do we go to church on Sunday?
text: Sunday is the day Jesus rose from the dead. That makes it the Lord's Day, a little Pascha every week, when we remember that Jesus is alive and has defeated death. The Church has gathered for worship on the first day of the week since the early days of the Apostles. On Sunday we pray together, hear the Gospel and receive Holy Communion in the Holy Liturgy. It is not just a rule. It is a happy family meeting where we meet Jesus, see our church friends and thank God for the whole week. Going every Sunday helps us grow closer to God, just as eating regularly helps our bodies grow.
