verse.text: This is the day which the LORD hath made; we will rejoice and be glad in it.

title: Why do we kiss the icons and the cross?
text: When we enter a church, many of us kiss the icons or the cross, or bow in front of them. We are not praying to wood or paint. Think of how you might kiss a photo of someone you love, like your grandmother. The kiss shows love and respect for the person in the picture, such as Jesus, St. Mary or a saint. The honor passes on to the one the icon shows. We also kiss the priest's hand cross when he blesses us. This is the way our church shows reverence and love. We worship God alone, and we honor the saints because they belong to Him and pray for us.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: Why do we ask the priest for a blessing?
text: After the Liturgy or when we meet Abouna, we often ask him for a blessing. The priest holds a cross, and we kiss it and his hand. The priest is not the source of the blessing. God is. Abouna is the servant of God who prays for us in the name of the Lord, and the hand cross reminds us of Jesus. It also shows respect and thankfulness for his work and his prayers for us. Children can do this too. It is a polite and holy greeting, and it helps us remember that God is always the one who blesses and protects us.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: The Jesus Prayer
text: The Jesus Prayer is a very short prayer that we can say anywhere, quietly in our hearts. The usual words are, Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, have mercy on me, a sinner. It is based on what the blind man Bartimaeus cried out to Jesus and on the prayer of the tax collector in Jesus's story. We can say it when we wake up, when we are walking, when we are scared, or when we cannot fall asleep. Saying it slowly helps us remember that Jesus is near and ready to help us. Some Orthodox Christians use a prayer rope to count them, but you do not need one. It is a good habit to start when you are young.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: Why do we pray towards the east?
text: In the Coptic Orthodox Church the altar is placed at the east end of the church, and the priest and people face east when they pray. Early Christians prayed this way. The east is where the sun rises, and it reminds us of Jesus, whom the Bible calls the Sun of righteousness, and of the light He brings to the world. It also reminds us of Eden, the garden God planted in the east, and our hope of returning to heaven. We also look forward to the second coming of Jesus. It is a special way to help us remember who we are praying to. At home you can pray facing east too, but God hears you in any direction.

verse.text: But unto you that fear my name shall the Sun of righteousness arise with healing in his wings;

title: Why do some people take their shoes off in church?
text: When God spoke to Moses at the burning bush, He told him to take his shoes off, because the ground was holy. In the same way, some Coptic churches have the custom of taking shoes off, or being very careful, in holy places, especially near the altar area, which is called the Haykal. It is a way to show respect and awe, because God is truly present there. Custom can be different from one church to another, so follow what your church and Abouna ask. Even when shoes stay on, we show respect by walking quietly, bowing and crossing ourselves. What matters most is a respectful heart.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

verse.text: put off thy shoes from off thy feet, for the place whereon thou standest is holy ground.

title: What are the Gospel and the Bible reading in church?
text: During the Holy Liturgy we listen to readings from the Bible. There are readings from the letters of the Apostles, from the Acts of the Apostles, from the Psalms and then the Gospel, which tells about the life and words of Jesus. When the Gospel is read, the deacons and the people stand, because we are listening to Jesus Himself speaking. The priest reads the Gospel and then often someone explains it in a sermon. The readings are chosen by the Church for each day, so we hear the whole Bible over time. Listening carefully and thinking about what we hear helps us live as God wants during the week.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: Why should we share?
text: Sharing means letting others use or have some of what we have, like a toy, a snack or our time. It can feel hard, but Jesus shared too. He shared five loaves and two fish with a huge crowd, and everyone had enough. When we share, we show love and make other people happy, and we remember that everything we have is a gift from God. The Bible says it is more blessed to give than to receive. You can share with your friends, your family, and with those in need through the church. Even a small share, like half your sandwich, makes a big difference.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

verse.text: It is more blessed to give than to receive.

title: Why do we obey our parents?
text: God gave us parents to love us, teach us and keep us safe. The Bible tells children to obey their parents in the Lord, and the Ten Commandments tell us to honor our father and mother. When we obey, we show love and respect, and we learn to listen to God too. Even Jesus, when He was a boy, obeyed St. Mary and St. Joseph. Obeying does not mean we are never allowed to ask questions or share how we feel. We can speak politely. Sometimes it is hard, and we make mistakes. When we do, we can say sorry and try again. God is pleased when we obey with a happy heart.

verse.text: Children, obey your parents in the Lord: for this is right.

title: How can I be brave?
text: Being brave does not mean you never feel afraid. It means doing the right thing even when you feel afraid. David was brave when he faced Goliath, Daniel was brave in the lions' den, and the martyrs were brave because they loved Jesus. Their courage came from trusting God, who was with them. When you feel scared at school, in the dark or at the doctor, you can pray, make the sign of the cross and say a short prayer like the Jesus Prayer. You can also tell a parent or a teacher how you feel. God promises to be with us, and that makes us strong.

verse.text: What time I am afraid, I will trust in thee.

title: Why does God let bad things happen?
text: This is a big question, and even grown ups wonder about it. God made the world good, and He gave people freedom to choose. Sometimes people choose wrong things, and the world has sickness and sadness because of sin. God does not cause evil. He is good, and He loves us. When bad things happen He is close to us and sad with us. Jesus wept when His friend died. God also comforts us through other people who help us, and He can bring good even out of hard times. We may not always understand why, but we can pray, tell a parent or Abouna how we feel, and trust that God never leaves us.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: Where is heaven?
text: Heaven is where God lives, and where the angels and the saints are with Him. It is a place of joy and light, with no sadness, sickness or fear. The Bible says Jesus went to prepare a place for us in His Father's house. We do not know exactly where heaven is or what it looks like, because it is bigger than anything we can imagine. We know that heaven is not far away from God's love, because God is with us now too. Everyone who loves Jesus and follows Him hopes to live with Him forever. We prepare for heaven by loving God, loving others and asking forgiveness when we do wrong.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

verse.text: In my Father's house are many mansions

title: Do angels watch over me?
text: Yes. The Bible says God sends His angels to take care of those who love Him. Our church teaches that each person has a guardian angel who looks after us, protects us and prays for us. Angels are God's messengers. We cannot see them, but they are near us, especially when we pray and when we are in church during the Liturgy. We can ask for the help of Archangel Michael, Archangel Gabriel and Archangel Raphael. We do not worship angels. We worship God alone. Angels help us because God asks them to. You can thank God for your guardian angel in your evening prayer.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

verse.text: For he shall give his angels charge over thee, to keep thee in all thy ways.

title: Why do we pray?
text: Praying is talking with God. He is our loving Father, and like any child who loves their family, we want to talk to Him. We can thank Him, say sorry, ask for help, and pray for other people. God already knows everything, but He loves to hear from us, and prayer draws us closer to Him. It also changes us. We become more kind, more peaceful and more thankful. We can pray anywhere and anytime, in our own words or with the prayers of the Church, like the Lord's Prayer and the Agpeya. We should pray in the morning, before meals, and before sleeping. Jesus Himself prayed often.

can i pray in my own words
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

verse.text: in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God.

title: Why should we read the Bible?
text: The Bible is God's word to us. It tells us who God is, how He made the world and how much He loves us. It tells the story of Jesus and teaches us how to live. When we read it, we get to know God better, just like getting to know a friend by listening to him. The Bible gives us comfort when we are sad, courage when we are afraid and wisdom when we need to choose. You can read a little each day, like a story from a children's Bible or a Gospel chapter, and ask Abouna or a servant when you do not understand something. It is like a lamp that lights our way.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

verse.text: Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path.

title: What is sin?
text: Sin is when we do something that goes against God's love, like lying, hurting someone, being greedy or disobeying on purpose. It can also be not doing the good we should do. Sin hurts us, other people and our friendship with God. Everyone makes mistakes and does wrong sometimes, even grown ups. But God does not stop loving us. That is why Jesus came, to save us and forgive us. When we sin, we can say sorry to God, say sorry to the person we hurt, and try to do better. In the sacrament of Confession the priest prays for us in God's name and we receive forgiveness.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

verse.text: For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God;

title: What is repentance?
text: Repentance means turning back to God. In Greek the word is metanoia, which means a change of mind and heart. When we do something wrong, we feel sorry, we say so to God, we decide to stop and we try to fix what we can. Then we do better. The story of the prodigal son shows repentance. He went back to his father, and his father ran to welcome him. God is like that father. He is always happy when we come back. We repent in our daily prayers and in the sacrament of Confession. Repenting is not only for big sins. It is a normal part of every Christian's life.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

verse.text: there is joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner that repenteth.

title: Being patient
text: Patience means waiting calmly without getting upset. It is hard to wait for a turn, for dinner, for a birthday or for someone to finish talking. The Bible shows people who waited for God, like Abraham, who waited for his son, and Noah, who waited for the flood to end. When we are patient, we show love, because we give other people time. We can practice patience by taking a slow breath, saying a short prayer and thinking of others. God is patient with us too. He waits for us to learn and grow, and does not give up on us. Ask Him to help you.

verse.text: Wait on the LORD: be of good courage, and he shall strengthen thine heart: wait, I say, on the LORD.

title: What is humility?
text: Humility means not thinking we are better than other people and remembering that all good things come from God. A humble person does not brag, and is happy to help, listen and say sorry. Jesus is our best example. He is God, yet He washed the feet of His disciples to show us how to serve. Humble people are not weak. They are strong because they know God is their helper. Saints like St. Antony and St. Moses the Black grew in humility, and God honored them. You can practice humility by thanking others, letting a friend go first and not boasting about winning.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

verse.text: Humble yourselves in the sight of the Lord, and he shall lift you up.

title: Does God hear me when I pray?
text: Yes, God always hears you. He hears every prayer, even a whisper or a prayer without words, and even if you pray in your heart at school. Jesus told us that God our Father knows what we need before we ask, and still He wants us to ask. Sometimes God answers right away, sometimes He asks us to wait, and sometimes the answer is different from what we hoped, because He sees what is best. When it seems He is not answering, we keep praying and trust that He loves us. We can also ask Abouna or a servant for help. You are never too small or too young for God to listen to you.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

verse.text: The righteous cry, and the LORD heareth, and delivereth them out of all their troubles.

title: Is God everywhere? Can He see me?
text: Yes. God is everywhere at the same time, and He loves us so much that He is always near. The Bible says nowhere can we go to be away from His presence. That means we are never alone, whether we are at home, at school, in the dark or in a hospital. God sees us, and not to catch us doing something wrong, but because He cares like a loving father. He sees our good deeds and our sadness too. Knowing He is close helps us make good choices and gives us comfort. We can talk to Him at any moment, with a short prayer in our heart.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

verse.text: Whither shall I go from thy spirit? or whither shall I flee from thy presence?

title: What if someone is mean to me?
text: It hurts when someone is unkind or teases us. First, remember that you are precious and loved by God. It is okay to tell a trusted grown up, like a parent, a teacher or Abouna, and it is okay to walk away. We should not hit back or say mean words. Jesus taught us to treat others the way we want to be treated, and to pray for those who are unkind. Praying for them does not mean what they did was okay. It means we ask God to help them change. If you see someone else being treated badly, be kind to that person and get help. Kindness is strong.

verse.text: Therefore all things whatsoever ye would that men should do to you, do ye even so to them

title: What happens when someone we love dies?
text: When someone we love dies, we feel very sad, and that is okay. Crying shows how much we loved them. As Christians we believe that Jesus defeated death when He rose from the dead, so death is not the end. The souls of those who loved God are in His care, and one day we will all be raised. In church we pray for those who have passed away, and we remember them with love. The Bible says God will wipe away every tear. If you are sad, talk to your parents or Abouna, pray, and remember the good times. God is close to those who are sad.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

verse.text: And God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes;

title: Who is St. Mark the Apostle?
text: St. Mark the Apostle brought the good news of Jesus to Egypt. He wrote the Gospel of Mark, and the Church teaches that he was the first Pope of Alexandria. That is why the Coptic Orthodox Church is called the Church of Alexandria, and why we are his spiritual children. Long ago he came to the great city of Alexandria, preached about Jesus, and many people believed and were baptized. He loved the people there, and he served them until the end of his life. Every time we go to church, we are part of the family that St. Mark began. We can thank God for him and ask for his prayers.

title: Who is St. Joseph the Carpenter?
text: St. Joseph was the righteous man who took care of St. Mary and baby Jesus. He worked hard as a carpenter. When an angel spoke to him in a dream, he listened to God and obeyed right away. He brought St. Mary and Jesus safely to Egypt, and later back home to Nazareth. He was gentle, quiet and trustworthy. The Church loves him as the guardian of the Holy Family. Joseph shows us that we can serve God by working honestly and by taking care of the people God gives us.

title: Who is St. John the Baptist?
text: St. John the Baptist was the cousin of Jesus. His parents were Zechariah and Elizabeth, and an angel told them about his birth. He lived simply and told people to turn back to God. His job was to get hearts ready for Jesus, so he is called the Forerunner. He baptized people in the Jordan River, and he baptized Jesus too. When he saw Jesus, he said Jesus is the Lamb of God. John was humble. He knew he was not the most important one, and he was happy to point to Jesus.

verse.text: Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world.

title: Who is St. Stephen?
text: St. Stephen was one of the first seven deacons of the Church. He was full of faith and the Holy Spirit, and he helped take care of widows and people in need. He spoke boldly about Jesus. Some people did not like this, and in the end he gave his life for Jesus. He is called the first martyr. Even then he was gentle: he prayed that God would forgive the people who were unkind to him. The Church calls him the Archdeacon, and the deacons in our church ask for his prayers. Stephen shows us how to forgive.

title: Who is St. Peter the Apostle?
text: Peter was a fisherman called Simon. Jesus called him to follow Him and said, I will make you a fisher of men. Peter was one of the twelve apostles, and he was often the first to speak up. He loved Jesus very much, but once he was afraid and said he did not know Jesus. Jesus forgave him and loved him again. After Pentecost, Peter preached boldly and many people believed. His story tells us that when we make mistakes, we can say sorry, and Jesus forgives us. The Church remembers him together with St. Paul at the Feast of the Apostles.

title: Who is St. Paul the Apostle?
text: Paul was first called Saul. At first he was against the followers of Jesus. Then Jesus appeared to him on the road to Damascus, and his life changed completely. He was baptized and became a great apostle. Paul traveled to many countries to tell people about Jesus, and he started many churches. He also wrote letters to them, called epistles, and many are in the New Testament. Paul went through many hard times, but he kept trusting God. He teaches us that anyone can change and serve Jesus with all their heart.

title: Who is St. George?
text: St. George was born in Cappadocia, and when he grew up he went to the emperor's court to take his father's place. There he saw that the emperor had turned against Jesus and ordered everyone to worship idols. George felt sad. He gave his money to the poor and set his servants free. He said no to the emperor and stayed faithful to Jesus, and the Lord gave him strength. He was kind and he was not afraid. The Church calls him the Prince of Martyrs. Many pictures show him on a horse, and many churches in Egypt and around the world are named for him. When we feel afraid to do what is right, we can remember St. George and ask for his prayers.

title: Who is St. Mina the Wonder Worker?
text: St. Mina was born in Egypt, and his mother had prayed to God for a child. When he grew up he was given an important job in his city. When the emperor ordered everyone to worship idols, Mina left his job and went to the desert to pray for many days. Then he came back to the city and bravely said that he believed in Jesus. The Church calls him the Wonder Worker, because many people were helped and healed through his prayers. His body was laid to rest in the Mariout area near Alexandria, and a big monastery of St. Mina stands there today. Many Coptic children are named Mina. When we are sick or worried, we can ask St. Mina to pray for us.

title: Who is St. Antony the Great?
text: St. Antony is called the Father of Monks. As a young man he heard the Gospel in church and wanted to follow Jesus with his whole heart. He gave what he had to the poor and went to the desert to pray. He lived simply and spent his time with God. Many people came to ask him for advice, and many became monks because of him. He showed us that prayer is powerful and that God is with us even in lonely places. His monastery near the Red Sea is still alive today.

title: Who is St. Pachomius?
text: St. Pachomius was born in Thebes in Upper Egypt, to parents who did not know Jesus. They wanted him to worship idols, but he refused. When he grew up he became a monk and learned the monk's life from St. Balamon. Later an angel told him to start a life where monks live together. Many monks gathered around him, and he built monasteries for them. He gave them a plan for working, praying and eating together. This is called community life, so he is called the Father of Community Life. He led the monks for forty years. He teaches us that we are stronger when we love, share and help each other.

title: Who is St. Macarius the Great?
text: St. Macarius the Great was a monk who lived in the desert of Scetis in Wadi El Natrun in Egypt. He loved to pray and was known for his kindness and his patience. Many people came to learn from him, and they say he had a gentle heart. A famous monastery is named after him in the same desert, and monks still pray there today. He teaches us to be patient, to pray often and to speak kindly to everyone.

title: Who is St. Moses the Black?
text: St. Moses the Black lived in Egypt long ago. Before he became a monk he did many wrong things. Then he heard about God's love, he said sorry from his heart and went to live in the desert of Scetis. He worked hard to become gentle and humble, and many people learned from him. He is a wonderful example of repentance, which means turning back to God. No one is too far away for God to forgive, and we can always begin again.

title: Who is St. Bishoy?
text: St. Bishoy was born in a town called Shansa in Egypt. The story says his mother saw an angel in a dream, who asked her to give one of her children to serve God. The angel chose Bishoy, even though he was thin and small. When he grew up he went to the desert of Shiheet and became a monk. He prayed and worked very hard, and God made him worthy to see the Lord Jesus. He also found a simple way to teach about the Holy Trinity, using a basket with three ears. He is often called the Perfect Man because of his love. St. Bishoy teaches us to serve God with all our heart.

title: Who is St. Shenouda the Archimandrite?
text: St. Shenouda the Archimandrite was born near Akhmim in Upper Egypt. He became the leader of a large monastery after Anba Bgoul. He followed the rules for community life that St. Pachomius wrote, and he added a promise that each monk had to make before joining. So many monks came to live there that the number reached 2200. The word Archimandrite means leader of the monks. He also went with St. Cyril to the Council of Ephesus. Before he died, he told his disciples to follow his steps and trusted them to God. St. Shenouda shows us that praying, working and living together in love make a strong family.

title: Who is St. Demiana?
text: St. Demiana lived in Egypt and gave her life to Jesus. She was the daughter of a governor, and she gathered forty young women who prayed and served God together with her. They were brave and loved each other, and they stayed faithful to Jesus even in hard times. The Church remembers them on the 13th of Tobi. There is a famous monastery of St. Demiana in the Delta, and many girls in Egypt are named after her. Their story shows us that good friends help each other love God.

title: Who is Archangel Michael?
text: The Archangel Michael is one of God's great angels. Angels are God's servants who are sent to help us. Michael is known as the protector of God's people, and the Church asks for his prayers every month on the 12th of the Coptic month. In the Bible he is a leader who stands up for the good. We cannot see angels, but God sends them to take care of us. We can pray, Archangel Michael, please pray for us, and we do not need to be afraid.

title: Who is Archangel Gabriel?
text: The Archangel Gabriel is the angel who brings good news. God sent him to tell Zechariah that he would have a son named John. Then God sent him to St. Mary in Nazareth to tell her that she would be the mother of Jesus. He said, Hail, full of grace, the Lord is with you. We remember his message every year at the Feast of the Annunciation. God sends us good news too, in the Bible and in prayer.

title: Who is St. Athanasius the Apostolic?
text: St. Athanasius was the 20th Pope of Alexandria, and he is called the Apostolic because he held to the faith of the apostles. When he was a young deacon, he went with his Pope to the Council of Nicea. There the Church taught clearly that Jesus Christ is truly God. Athanasius kept teaching this faith, even when powerful people were against him and he was sent away several times. Because of him, the Church is strong in the true faith. He teaches us to stand for what is true with love and courage.

title: Who is St. Cyril the Great?
text: St. Cyril was the 24th Pope of Alexandria and is called the Pillar of the Faith. He defended the teaching that St. Mary is truly the Theotokos, which means the Mother of God, because the child she carried is God the Son. This was affirmed at the Council of Ephesus. Cyril wrote many books explaining the faith, and the Church still loves them. When we sing praises to St. Mary, we remember how Cyril and the Church honored her.

title: Who is St. Mary of Egypt?
text: St. Mary of Egypt lived long ago. In her young life she was far from God. Then, during a visit to Jerusalem, she was moved to pray and she decided to change. She went into the desert beyond the Jordan River and lived there in prayer for many years. A priest named Zosimas met her near the end of her life. The Church remembers her on the 6th of Baramouda. St. Mary of Egypt reminds us that no matter what has happened, God welcomes everyone who turns back to Him with all their heart.

title: Who is St. Abanoub?
text: St. Abanoub was a young boy who loved Jesus very much. He was born in the town of Nehisa in Egypt, and his parents taught him to love God and to be kind. When he was about twelve years old, he gave his money to the poor and bravely said that he believed in Jesus, even though it was not easy. He kept loving Jesus until the end. The Church remembers him on the 24th of Abib, and his body rests in his church in Samanoud. Many children are named Abanoub. He shows us that children can be heroes of faith too.

title: Who is Pope Kyrillos VI?
text: Pope Kyrillos VI was the 116th Pope of Alexandria. Before he became Pope, he was a monk named Father Mina, who lived a simple life of prayer. He loved the Holy Liturgy and prayed it very often. He was Pope from 1959 until 1971, and he cared for the Church with much love and prayer. He also took care of the monastery of St. Mina in Mariout, where he is buried. Many people say that they were helped through his prayers. He teaches us that prayer is very strong, and that a humble heart is dear to God.

title: Who was Pope Shenouda III?
text: Pope Shenouda III was the 117th Pope of Alexandria. When he was sixteen he began to serve in Sunday School, and he kept teaching children for many years. Later he became a monk and lived in the desert of Wadi El Natrun. Then he became a bishop whose work was Christian education, and in 1971 he became Pope. He served the Church for about forty one years and wrote more than one hundred books. Many Copts remember him with love and respect. He reminds us to love the Bible and to keep learning about God.

title: Who are the 21 Martyrs of Libya?
text: The 21 Martyrs of Libya were twenty one men who loved Jesus very much. They were Coptic Orthodox Christians, and they were working far from home. Because they believed in Jesus, they were asked to say that they did not, but they kept their faith and said His name. Our Church remembers them as saints, and we pray that they pray for us. They remind us that loving Jesus is the most important thing in the world, and that God holds His children close.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary, Synaxarium style

title: Who is Anba Abraam of Fayoum?
text: Anba Abraam was the bishop of Fayoum in Egypt. He lived in the 1800s and passed away in 1914, more than a hundred years ago. He loved the poor so much that he is called the Friend of the Poor. When he led a monastery, it became a safe place for thousands of poor people. As a bishop, he gave away everything he received, helped people with food and clothes, and let many poor people stay at his home. He prayed a lot. His example shows us that giving to others with a happy heart is one way to love Jesus.

title: Who is St. John the Beloved?
text: St. John was one of the twelve apostles, and he is called the disciple whom Jesus loved. He stayed close to Jesus, even at the Cross, where Jesus asked him to care for St. Mary. John wrote the Gospel of John and three letters, and the book of Revelation. He taught that God is love, and that we should love one another. John teaches us to stay near to Jesus and to love others as He does.

verse.text: God is love.

title: Who is Archangel Raphael?
text: The Archangel Raphael is an angel who helps and heals. His name means God heals. In the book of Tobit, he walked with a young man named Tobias on a long journey, kept him safe and helped him and his family. The Church remembers Raphael as a helper in times of sickness and a guide in danger. We can ask him to pray for us and for people who are ill. God cares about us and sends His angels to watch over us.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary, Synaxarium style

title: Who is St. Philopater Mercurius?
text: St. Philopater Mercurius was born in Rome to Christian parents, and his name means lover of the Father. When he grew up he became a soldier in the army. The story says an angel gave him a sword and told him to remember the Lord God whenever he won against his enemies. That is why he is called Abu Seifein, which means the one with two swords: one for the army and one for the power of God. He would not honor the idols, and he stayed faithful to Jesus. He teaches us to be loyal to Jesus, no matter what.

title: What is the Feast of Nayrouz?
text: Nayrouz is the Coptic New Year. It begins on the first day of the month of Tout, which is usually September 11 or 12 in our calendar. The Coptic calendar began in the time of Emperor Diocletian, when many Christians were martyred. So we also call it the Era of the Martyrs, and we remember them with thankfulness. It is a time to start fresh, to thank God for another year and to ask for blessings and peace. In the Church we pray special hymns, and many families celebrate with joy.

title: What is the Feast of the Cross?
text: The Feast of the Cross reminds us of the cross of Jesus. On the cross, Jesus gave His life out of love for us, and then He rose again. For us the cross is a sign of love and victory. We make the sign of the cross when we pray. Queen Helena, the mother of Emperor Constantine, found the Cross in Jerusalem and built a church for it. We celebrate the church of the Cross on the 17th of Tout, and the appearance of the Cross on the 10th of Baramhat. We love the cross because it shows how much Jesus loves us.

verse.text: For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.

title: What is the Annunciation?
text: The Annunciation is the day we remember when the angel Gabriel visited St. Mary. He told her that God had chosen her to be the mother of Jesus. St. Mary was humble and she said yes. She said, Let it be to me according to your word. We celebrate this feast every year on the 29th of Baramhat, and it is a happy day. It teaches us to say yes to God, too.

title: What is Christmas, the Nativity of Jesus?
text: The Nativity is the birthday of Jesus. We celebrate it with the Church on January 7, which is the 29th of Koiahk in the Coptic calendar. Jesus was born in Bethlehem, in a simple place, to St. Mary and with St. Joseph beside her. Angels told shepherds the good news, and wise men later came to see Him. God became a little baby because He loves us. We celebrate with the Holy Liturgy, with hymns and with joy.

title: What is Epiphany, the Feast of Theophany?
text: Theophany means God shows Himself. It is the feast when Jesus was baptized by John in the Jordan River. The Holy Spirit came down like a dove, and the voice of the Father said, This is My beloved Son. So all three Persons of the Holy Trinity were shown. In the Coptic Church the feast is celebrated on the 11th of Tobi, which is usually January 19. It also reminds us of our own baptism.

title: What is the Presentation of Jesus in the Temple?
text: When Jesus was a baby, St. Mary and St. Joseph brought Him to the temple in Jerusalem, as the law taught. There an old man named Simeon took Him in his arms and thanked God. Simeon had been waiting to see the promised Savior, and he said that Jesus is a light to all nations. A prophetess named Anna also praised God. We celebrate this feast on the 8th of Amshir. It teaches us to give our best to God.

title: Why do we celebrate the Entry of Jesus into Egypt?
text: When Jesus was a small child, an angel warned St. Joseph in a dream to take Jesus and St. Mary to Egypt. So the Holy Family traveled to Egypt and stayed for a time, until it was safe to go back to Nazareth. Coptic tradition remembers many places in Egypt that they visited, and many churches stand there today. We celebrate this feast on the 24th of Bashans, and Egypt is called blessed because Jesus walked on its land. The prophet Isaiah said, Blessed be Egypt My people.

title: What is Palm Sunday?
text: Palm Sunday is the day Jesus rode into Jerusalem on a donkey. The people were so happy to see Him! They waved palm branches and shouted, Hosanna, which means save us. They welcomed Him as their King. In church we hold palms and sing happy hymns, and the priest prays for us. Palm Sunday is the start of Holy Week.

title: What is Holy Week and Pascha?
text: Holy Week is the week before Easter, and we call it Pascha. We pray special prayers each day in church and remember the last days of Jesus on earth. On Covenant Thursday we remember the Last Supper, when Jesus gave us the Eucharist, and He washed the disciples' feet. On Good Friday we remember His crucifixion, and we pray quietly and with deep love. On Saturday evening we get ready for the joy of the Resurrection. It is a serious week, but it ends with great joy.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: What is the Ascension of Jesus?
text: Forty days after His Resurrection, Jesus went up to heaven in front of His disciples. A cloud received Him, and angels told them that He will come again in the same way. Jesus did not leave us alone. He promised to send the Holy Spirit, and He sits at the right hand of the Father. We celebrate Ascension on a Thursday, forty days after Easter. It teaches us that heaven is our home, and that Jesus is always with us.

title: What is Pentecost?
text: Pentecost is the feast of the coming of the Holy Spirit. It is fifty days after the Resurrection. The disciples were praying together in Jerusalem, and the Holy Spirit came upon them like tongues of fire. They began to speak in many languages and told people about Jesus, and many were baptized that day. We call it the birthday of the Church. The Holy Spirit helps us to pray, to love and to do what is right.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: What is the Transfiguration?
text: One day Jesus took Peter, James and John up a high mountain. There His face shone like the sun, and His clothes became bright as light. Moses and Elijah appeared and spoke with Him. A voice from the cloud said, This is My beloved Son, listen to Him. The disciples saw some of His glory. The Church celebrates this feast on the 13th of Mesra. It teaches us that Jesus is God, and that we should listen to Him.

title: What is the Feast of St. Mary's Departure?
text: The Church remembers when St. Mary, the Theotokos, finished her life on earth. We say that she fell asleep in peace, and the Church teaches that the Lord took her to be with Him. The Church remembers her departure on the 21st of Tobi, and the taking of her body on the 16th of Mesra. Fifteen days before this second feast, many Copts fast to honor her. We love St. Mary as our mother in faith, and we ask for her prayers.

title: What is the Wedding at Cana?
text: Jesus went with St. Mary and His disciples to a wedding in a town called Cana. During the wedding, the family ran out of wine. St. Mary told the servants, Do whatever He tells you. Jesus asked them to fill big jars with water, and the water became wine. It was His first miracle. The Church celebrates this feast on the 13th of Tobi. Jesus cares about our needs, and St. Mary helps us ask Him.

title: What is the Finding of the Cross?
text: The Cross of Jesus was hidden for a long time. St. Helena, the mother of Emperor Constantine, was a devout Christian who wanted to find it. The Church remembers that she traveled to Jerusalem, and the Cross was found there, and a church was built on that holy place. We celebrate the finding of the Cross on the 10th of Baramhat. It reminds us to treasure the Cross, and to be thankful for the love of Jesus.

title: What is the Feast of the Apostles?
text: The Feast of the Apostles remembers St. Peter and St. Paul, who preached about Jesus in Rome and loved Him until the end of their lives. Peter was a fisherman from Bethsaida, and Paul was born in Tarsus. The twelve apostles left everything to follow Jesus, and after Pentecost they went out to tell the world about Him. We would not know Jesus today without them. The feast is on the 5th of Abib, at the end of the Apostles Fast. We thank God for their courage and ask for their prayers.

title: What is the Circumcision of Jesus?
text: Eight days after He was born, Jesus was circumcised, as the law of Moses taught, and He was given the name Jesus. His name means the Lord saves. The angel had told St. Mary and St. Joseph to give Him this name. It shows that Jesus came to keep the law, and not to break it. The Church remembers this on the 6th of Tobi. It teaches us to honor the name of Jesus.

title: What is the Nativity Fast?
text: The Nativity Fast helps us get ready for Christmas. It begins on the 16th of Hatour and ends on the 28th of Koiahk, just before the Feast of the Nativity. During the fast we eat plant-based food and pray more. The month of Koiahk is full of lovely hymns for St. Mary. Fasting teaches us to wait with love, to share with others and to think about Jesus.

title: What is the Apostles Fast?
text: The Apostles Fast begins on the Monday after Pentecost and finishes the day before the Feast of the Apostles, the 5th of Abib. The length changes every year, because it depends on the date of Easter. The apostles fasted and prayed before they went to preach, and we follow their example. During the fast we eat plant based foods and pray more. It reminds us to be thankful for the apostles.

title: What is the Fast of St. Mary?
text: The Fast of St. Mary lasts fifteen days, from the first until the fifteenth of the month of Mesra, which is in August. It leads to the Feast of St. Mary's taking up to heaven, on the 16th of Mesra. We eat plant based food and pray more, and many people sing hymns of praise to her. We fast with love for St. Mary, and she prays for us. It is a joyful and peaceful fast.

title: What is the Fast of Nineveh?
text: The Fast of Nineveh is a three day fast about two weeks before Great Lent. We remember the prophet Jonah, whom God sent to the people of Nineveh. They listened, they fasted and prayed, and they turned away from doing wrong. God saw this and forgave them. The fast reminds us that God is merciful, and that He loves it when people say sorry. It also gets us ready for Great Lent.

title: Who is St. Paul the First Hermit?
text: St. Paul the First Hermit lived in the Egyptian desert long ago. As a young man he left his home because it was dangerous to follow Jesus in those days. He found a cave in the desert and decided to give his whole life to prayer. Tradition says a palm tree gave him food and clothes, and a spring gave him water. Each day a raven brought him half a loaf of bread. He lived this way for many years, and the world almost forgot him. Then St. Antony came looking for him, and the two saints met and shared a meal. Soon after, Paul went to be with Jesus, and St. Antony buried him. We remember St. Paul as the first monk in the desert, who loved to pray and trusted God to take care of him.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary, Synaxarium style

title: Who is St. Samuel the Confessor?
text: St. Samuel the Confessor was a monk who lived in Egypt hundreds of years ago. He loved God and went to the desert to pray and learn from wise older monks. Later he became the leader of a monastery at Mount Qalamoun, in the desert. He is called a Confessor because he stayed faithful to the true faith of the Church, even when people hurt him and troubled him for it. He did not give up and he did not stop trusting Jesus. Many monks learned from his love, his patience and his courage. His monastery is still there today, and people visit it to pray. We remember him when we need to be brave about our faith.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary, Synaxarium style

title: Who is St. Barbara?
text: St. Barbara was a young woman who lived long ago. Her father did not believe in Jesus, but Barbara learned about Jesus and loved Him with all her heart. She was baptized and she would not stop believing, even when her father was angry and tried to change her mind. Barbara stayed gentle and brave. Because she loved Jesus so much, she never gave up her faith, and the Church honors her as a martyr. The Church remembers her with St. Juliana on the same day in the Synaxarium. When we feel afraid to say that we love Jesus, we can ask St. Barbara to pray for us to be brave.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary, Synaxarium style

title: Who is St. Verena?
text: St. Verena is a saint who came from Egypt. Tradition says she was a nurse who followed a group of Christian soldiers from Egypt all the way to the land that is now Switzerland. There she lived a quiet life of prayer and kindness. She cared for people who were sick and helped the poor, and she taught people to keep clean and to love one another. Because of her, many people there learned about Jesus. She reminds us that a Christian from Egypt can bless people in far away countries. We remember St. Verena when we want to help people who are sick or in need.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary, Synaxarium style

title: Who are the 49 Martyrs of Shiyyat (Scetis)?
text: The 49 Martyrs were holy elder monks who lived in the desert of Shiyyat, also called Scetis, in Egypt. They lived simple lives of prayer, fasting and kindness. One day raiders attacked the monastery. The old monks did not run away from Jesus. They stayed together and kept praying, and they went to heaven together. The Church honors them as martyrs and remembers them every year. Their relics, which are their holy bodies, are kept in the Monastery of St. Macarius in Wadi El Natrun. They teach us that love for Jesus is stronger than fear, and that it is good to stay together in prayer.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary, Synaxarium style

title: Who are the Three Holy Youths?
text: The Three Holy Youths were Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego. They lived in the land of Babylon with the prophet Daniel. The king made a big golden statue and told everyone to bow down to it. The three friends said no. They would only worship the one true God. The king was angry and had them put into a very hot furnace. But God was with them! The king looked in and saw a fourth person walking with them, and he looked like the Son of God. The three friends came out safe, without even the smell of smoke. We remember them when we are asked to do something wrong. God is always with us.

title: Who are the Forty Martyrs of Sebaste?
text: The Forty Martyrs were forty brave soldiers in the Roman army. They loved Jesus and would not say that they did not believe in Him. As a test, they were told to stand out in the cold on a frozen lake. They stayed there together and prayed, and they encouraged each other to be strong. The story says that one soldier gave up, but one of the guards saw how brave they were and joined them, so there were still forty. The Church honors them as martyrs. They teach us how powerful it is to be brave together and to help each other stay close to Jesus.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary, Synaxarium style

title: Who is St. Elizabeth?
text: St. Elizabeth was the wife of Zacharias the priest and the mother of St. John the Baptist. She and Zacharias loved God, but they had no children and they were very old. God sent a miracle and gave them a baby boy. When the Virgin Mary came to visit her cousin Elizabeth, the baby in Elizabeth's womb jumped for joy, and Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit. She called Mary the mother of her Lord. Elizabeth teaches us to be patient and to trust that God hears our prayers at the right time. She was very happy to welcome Mary, and we should be happy to welcome others too.

verse.text: Blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb.

title: Who is Zacharias the Priest?
text: Zacharias was a priest in the temple in Jerusalem, and the father of St. John the Baptist. One day, while he was burning incense in the temple, the Archangel Gabriel appeared to him. Gabriel said that Zacharias and his wife Elizabeth would have a baby boy, and his name would be John. Zacharias found it hard to believe because they were old, so he could not speak until the baby was born. When the family asked what to name the baby, Zacharias wrote John, and right away he could speak again. He praised God with a beautiful song. His story teaches us that nothing is too hard for God.

title: Who is St. Simeon the Elder?
text: Simeon was a good and faithful old man who lived in Jerusalem. God had promised him that he would see the Savior before he died. One day the Holy Spirit led him to the temple, just when Mary and Joseph brought the baby Jesus to present Him to God. Simeon took Jesus in his arms and thanked God. He said he could now go in peace because he had seen the salvation God had prepared for all people. He also told Mary that she would have sorrow, like a sword going through her heart. Simeon teaches us to wait for God with patience and joy. The Church remembers him at the Feast of the Presentation.

title: Who are St. Joachim and St. Anna?
text: St. Joachim and St. Anna are remembered by the Church as the parents of the Virgin Mary, which makes them the grandparents of Jesus according to His human nature. The Bible does not tell us their story. Church tradition says they were holy people who loved God and prayed for a child for many years. They are honored for raising Mary in a home full of prayer and love. Because of this, the Church holds them in great respect. They teach parents and grandparents how important it is to pray with children and teach them to love God.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary, Synaxarium style

title: Who is St. Mary Magdalene?
text: Mary Magdalene was a woman who followed Jesus and loved Him very much. Jesus had healed her, and she stayed close to Him and helped Him. She stood near the cross when Jesus died. Very early on Sunday morning she went to the tomb with spices, and she found it empty. She was crying, but Jesus Himself appeared to her and called her by her name, Mary. She was the first to see the risen Lord, and Jesus sent her to tell the disciples the good news. The Church calls her and the other women who came to the tomb the myrrh-bearing women. She teaches us to love Jesus and to tell others that He is risen.

title: Who is St. Andrew the Apostle?
text: St. Andrew was a fisherman and the brother of St. Peter. He first followed St. John the Baptist, and when John pointed to Jesus, Andrew went to Jesus and stayed with Him that day. Then he ran to tell his brother Peter that they had found the Messiah, and he brought Peter to Jesus. Andrew loved to bring people to Jesus. When a crowd was hungry, it was Andrew who told Jesus about a boy with five loaves and two fish. Church tradition says he later preached the Gospel in faraway lands. He teaches us that we can bring our friends and family to Jesus, and that even small things can help when we give them to Him.

title: Who is St. James, son of Zebedee?
text: St. James was a fisherman and the brother of St. John the Beloved. Their father was Zebedee. When Jesus called them by the lake, they left their boat and nets and followed Him right away. Jesus gave James and John the nickname Sons of Thunder. James was one of the three disciples who were with Jesus at the Transfiguration. After the Ascension, James preached about Jesus in Jerusalem. The Book of Acts tells us he was the first of the apostles to give his life for Jesus. The Church honors him as an apostle and a martyr. He teaches us to answer Jesus when He calls and to follow Him bravely.

title: Who is St. Thomas the Apostle?
text: St. Thomas was one of the twelve apostles. After Jesus rose from the dead, He appeared to the disciples, but Thomas was not there. When they told him, Thomas said he could not believe it until he saw the marks of the nails himself. A week later Jesus came again and invited Thomas to touch His hands and His side. Thomas bowed and said, My Lord and my God! Jesus said that those who believe without seeing are blessed. That is us! Church tradition says Thomas later carried the Gospel far away, to India. Thomas teaches us that it is okay to ask questions, and that Jesus is patient with us.

verse.text: Thomas answered and said unto him, My Lord and my God.

title: Who is St. Matthew the Apostle?
text: St. Matthew, also called Levi, was a tax collector. Many people did not like tax collectors, because they often took too much money. One day Jesus walked by and said to Matthew, Follow Me. Matthew got up, left his table and followed Jesus at once. He even invited Jesus to a big meal in his house with many friends. Jesus showed that He came to call sinners to repentance and that He loves everyone. Later Matthew wrote the first Gospel in the New Testament, which tells how Jesus is the promised Messiah. Matthew teaches us that Jesus can change anyone, and that we should say yes quickly when He calls.

title: Who is St. Luke the Evangelist?
text: St. Luke was a doctor who became a follower of Jesus and a friend and helper of St. Paul. Under the guidance of the Holy Spirit, he wrote two books in the New Testament, the Gospel of Luke and the Acts of the Apostles. In his Gospel he tells us many stories we love, like the birth of Jesus, the good Samaritan, the lost sheep and the prodigal son. He also carefully wrote about the Virgin Mary. Church tradition says Luke also painted an icon of St. Mary. Luke teaches us to use our skills to help others and to write and tell the good news about Jesus.

title: Who is St. Barnabas?
text: Barnabas was an early Christian whose name means Son of Encouragement. He sold a field and gave the money to the apostles to help the poor. When St. Paul first came to Jerusalem after becoming a Christian, many were afraid of him, but Barnabas welcomed Paul and took him to the apostles. Later Barnabas and Paul traveled together to teach about Jesus. Barnabas also gave a second chance to his young cousin John Mark, who later wrote the Gospel and is St. Mark the Apostle. Barnabas teaches us to encourage others, to be generous, and to give people a second chance.

title: Who is St. Lazarus?
text: Lazarus lived in the town of Bethany with his sisters Martha and Mary. Jesus loved this family and often visited them. When Lazarus became sick and died, his sisters were very sad. Jesus came, and He cried with them, because He loves us and cares when we are sad. Then He went to the tomb and called with a loud voice, Lazarus, come out! And Lazarus came out alive. Everyone saw that Jesus has power over death. The Church remembers this miracle on Lazarus Saturday, the day before Palm Sunday. It also shows us that one day Jesus will raise everyone.

verse.text: Jesus wept.

title: Who is Zacchaeus?
text: Zacchaeus was a short man who collected taxes in the city of Jericho. He had a lot of money, but he was not happy, and people did not like him. One day he heard that Jesus was coming. He wanted to see Jesus, but the crowd was big and he was too short. So he ran ahead and climbed a sycamore tree! When Jesus came by, He looked up and said, Zacchaeus, come down. Today I will stay at your house. Zacchaeus was so happy! He promised to give half of his money to the poor and to give back what he had taken. Jesus loves to visit hearts that welcome Him.

title: Who is St. Basil the Great?
text: St. Basil the Great was a bishop of Caesarea, a city in what is now Turkey. He was very wise and learned, and he loved the poor. He helped build places to care for sick and hungry people. He also taught about the Holy Trinity and wrote prayers for the Church. One of the most important is the Liturgy of St. Basil, which we pray in the Coptic Church, especially during seasons like Lent and Advent. Many of its prayers are said by the priest while the people answer together. Because the Church of Alexandria honors him, we remember him as one of the great teachers of the faith. He teaches us to love God and to take care of people in need.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary, Synaxarium style

title: Who is St. Gregory the Theologian?
text: St. Gregory is called the Theologian because he spoke and wrote so well about God. He was a bishop and a very good teacher in the fourth century. He taught clearly that the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit are one God, the Holy Trinity. The Church honors him for his wisdom and his holy life. One of the three Liturgies of the Coptic Church is named after him, the Liturgy of St. Gregory, and it is often prayed on feasts of our Lord. When we pray it, we remember to thank God for the teachers who passed the faith to us. St. Gregory teaches us to learn about God with love and humility.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary, Synaxarium style

title: Who is Pope Dioscorus of Alexandria?
text: Pope Dioscorus was a Pope of Alexandria in the fifth century, after St. Cyril the Great. He loved the Church and its teaching, and he worked hard to protect the faith that the Church of Alexandria received from the apostles. When great disagreements came, he stayed faithful to what he believed was the true faith and did not give in, even though he suffered for it. He was sent away from Alexandria into exile and was far from his people. The Coptic Church honors him as a saint and as a defender of the faith. He teaches us to hold on to the faith with love and courage.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary, Synaxarium style

title: Who is St. Arsenius the Teacher of the Kings' Sons?
text: St. Arsenius lived a very comfortable life in the palace of the emperor. He was a teacher of the emperor's sons and had everything he wanted. But he heard a voice inside him saying that he should leave the world and be saved. So he left the palace and went to live as a monk in the desert of Scetis in Egypt. He gave up his rich clothes and learned to live simply, and he loved quiet and prayer. He was known to say that it is good to flee, to be silent and to pray. He teaches us that being close to God is more important than having riches or being important.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary, Synaxarium style

title: Who is St. John the Short?
text: St. John the Short, or John the Dwarf, was a small man who became a great monk in the desert of Scetis in Egypt. He came to the desert as a young man and was a student of an old monk. To test his obedience, the old monk gave him a dry stick and told him to water it every day. The water was far away, and the walk was long, but John did it with love for years. Then the stick grew into a tree and bore fruit! The old man shared the fruit with the other monks, saying it was the fruit of obedience. John teaches us to listen, to work with a happy heart and to be humble.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary, Synaxarium style

title: Who is Pope Peter, the Seal of the Martyrs?
text: Pope Peter was a Pope of Alexandria at the time of the great persecutions of Christians, the Era of the Martyrs. He loved his flock, the people of the Church, and prayed for them and taught them to stay strong. He is called the Seal of the Martyrs, because he is remembered as the last of the Popes of Alexandria to give his life for Christ in that age. Soon after, the persecutions ended and the Church could pray in peace. He teaches us how much the early Christians loved Jesus, and how thankful we should be that we can pray in church freely.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary, Synaxarium style

title: Who is Pope Kyrillos IV, the Father of Reform?
text: Pope Kyrillos IV was the Pope of Alexandria in the nineteenth century. He is called the Father of Reform because he worked to renew the Church. He loved learning, and he opened schools for boys and girls so that Coptic children could be educated. He also brought a printing press to Egypt so that church books could be printed. He worked to make the Church stronger and to help the people. He did not have a long time as Pope, but his work helped the Church for many years. He teaches us to love school and learning, and to use what we learn to serve God and the Church.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary, Synaxarium style

title: Who is St. Catherine of Alexandria?
text: St. Catherine was a young woman from the city of Alexandria, the same city where St. Mark preached. She was very clever and studied hard. Church tradition tells that she talked with many wise teachers and showed them that Jesus is the true God, and some of them believed in Him because of her. Because she would not give up her faith, she became a martyr. The Church honors her as a saint and a martyr. St. Catherine shows us that learning and faith go together, and that we can use our minds to love and explain the faith kindly.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary, Synaxarium style

title: Who is St. Philip the Apostle?
text: St. Philip was one of the twelve apostles, from the town of Bethsaida, the same town as Peter and Andrew. When Jesus found him, He said, Follow Me. Philip followed Jesus and was so happy that he went to find his friend Nathanael to tell him about Jesus. Nathanael wasn't sure, and Philip simply said, Come and see. That is a great way to share Jesus: invite a friend to come and see. Philip was also one of the disciples Jesus asked about food before feeding the five thousand. Church tradition says he preached the Gospel in other lands. Philip teaches us to invite our friends to come and see Jesus in church.

verse.text: Come and see.

title: Who is the Prophet Elijah?
text: Elijah was a brave prophet of God who lived in Israel. When the people had stopped worshiping the true God, Elijah told them to come back. God took care of him in hard times. Once ravens brought him bread and meat, and once a poor widow shared her last bit of flour and oil, and God made them last. On Mount Carmel, Elijah prayed and fire came down from heaven, showing that the Lord is the only true God. At the end of his life, God took Elijah up to heaven in a chariot of fire. Many years later he appeared with Moses at the Transfiguration of Jesus. Elijah teaches us to be brave and to trust God.

title: Who is St. John Chrysostom?
text: St. John Chrysostom lived in the fourth century and became the bishop of Constantinople. His name Chrysostom means golden mouth, because he was a wonderful preacher. When he spoke, people loved listening. He taught about the Bible and about how to live as a Christian. He cared especially for the poor and spoke out when people were unkind. Because he said hard things that people didn't always want to hear, he was sent away from his church, but he kept loving God and his people. The Church remembers him as a great teacher, and we pray prayers connected with him. He teaches us to use our words well, to teach about Jesus and to be kind to the poor.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary, Synaxarium style

title: Who is St. Timothy?
text: St. Timothy was a young helper of St. Paul. He learned about God from his mother Eunice and his grandmother Lois, who taught him the holy Scriptures from when he was little. Paul met Timothy on his journeys and loved him like a son. Timothy traveled with Paul and helped to teach and encourage new Christians. Paul wrote two letters to him, which are in the New Testament. In them Paul tells Timothy not to let anyone look down on him because he is young. Church tradition says Timothy became a bishop. He teaches kids that even young people can serve God and be good examples.

verse.text: Let no man despise thy youth; but be thou an example of the believers.

title: Who is St. Matthias the Apostle?
text: After Judas left the apostles, there were only eleven of them. The apostles prayed to know who God wanted to take his place. They looked for a man who had been with Jesus from the beginning, from His baptism until His Ascension. Two men were chosen as possible names, and the apostles prayed and cast lots. The choice fell on Matthias, and he was counted with the twelve apostles. After Pentecost he preached the Gospel. Matthias teaches us that God has a plan for His Church, and that He can use anyone who has been faithful, even if the person is not famous.

title: Who are Martha and Mary of Bethany?
text: Martha and Mary were sisters who lived in Bethany, and Jesus loved them. When Jesus came to visit, Martha worked hard in the kitchen to get everything ready, and she was a little upset. Her sister Mary sat down next to Jesus to listen to His words. Jesus told Martha gently that Mary had chosen the good part, which was to listen to Him. Martha loved Jesus, too, and later she said that she believed Jesus was the Son of God. Their brother was Lazarus. Their story teaches us that it is good to serve, but it is best to spend time with Jesus first.

title: Who are St. Joseph of Arimathea and St. Nicodemus?
text: Joseph of Arimathea and Nicodemus were two members of the Jewish council who believed in Jesus, but they had been afraid to say so. After Jesus died on the cross, they were not afraid anymore. Joseph went to Pilate and bravely asked for the body of Jesus. Nicodemus brought a large amount of spices. Together they took the body of Jesus down from the cross, wrapped it in clean linen with the spices, and laid it in Joseph's new tomb. The Church remembers them with love every Holy Week. They teach us that it is never too late to show our love for Jesus and to be brave.
